📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the Grand Theft Auto games have always been synonymous with America; Americana is baked into the crime series' very being. Across its history, there's only ever been one GTA game set outside America: the London-based expansion of the original game.

GTA 6 follows this template, parodying the American state of Florida and the city of Miami. But what about the next game - will the series always be in America? Not necessarily.

In an interview with The Guardian, Rockstar North co-studio boss Rob Nelson propped the proverbial door open a sliver by saying: "Never say never." He then rapidly followed that comment with: "But there’s still so much to do in America".

This is a topic Rockstar has responded to before, most notably when company co-founder and long-time GTA writer Dan Houser - who's no longer at Rockstar - discussed why the series always seemed to return to America. He said it was because cities like Miami and Latest York and Los Angeles are places where extreme juxtapositions exist. They're places where extreme wealth rubs shoulders with extreme poverty, and where organised crime can be found.

There's also something America infamously has that few other countries do, and that's free availability of guns, which is such a core tenet of a GTA experience.

Nevertheless, Obbe Vermeij - a former technical director at Rockstar North - revealed last year that a GTA: Tokyo almost happened. However, it wasn't going to be made by Rockstar but rather an external team in Japan.

Industry observers note that while discussing the subject, Vermeij referred to America as "basically the epicenter of Western culture". "Everybody knows the cities, even people who haven't been there," Vermeij said. "They have a mental image of the cities. I'm afraid we're stuck in this loop of about five American cities. Let's just get used to it.".

Industry observers note that GTA 6 is just days away from its 19th November release on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. Rockstar recently clarified the game runs at 30FPS across all platforms and confirmed that while it's available through Xbox Cloud Gaming, it cannot be streamed to PCs or non-Xbox devices.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, I've had my eye on TCL CSOT—CSOT being a TCL subsidiary responsible for OLED production—for a while now.
  • It has been revealed that according to Display Specifications (via TechPowerUp), at the Display Tech-Ecosystem Conference 2026 (DTC2026), TCL CSOT showed off a 27-inch, 1440p, 500 Hz gaming monitor made using IJP tech.
  • It has been revealed that you already knew what that was, right?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, I've had my eye on TCL CSOT—CSOT being a TCL subsidiary responsible for OLED production—for a while now. It might just be the company that brings OLED monitor prices down thanks to its use of the inkjet-printing (IJP) process in manufacturing. TCL CSOT had already noted it was moving in equipment for IJP manufacturing and expected production in the fourth quarter of 2027, but the company is now showing off some pretty impressive panels made using the process.

It has been revealed that according to Display Specifications (via TechPowerUp), at the Display Tech-Ecosystem Conference 2026 (DTC2026), TCL CSOT showed off a 27-inch, 1440p, 500 Hz gaming monitor made using IJP tech. Apparently, the company describes this monitor as having the "world's first high-refresh-rate in-panel compensation system.".

It has been revealed that you already knew what that was, right? No, me either. According to Display Specification's understanding of the announcement, it's tech that "continuously adjusts image performance in the background without requiring periodic compensation cycles while the display is powered off.".

OLED pixels can degrade at different rates, which is what causes pixel burn-in. The usual method for solving this is to run compensation cycles while the display is off, which takes a few minutes and boosts underperforming pixels up a bit back to where they should be.

It sounds like TCL's fresh tech will somehow allow this to happen without turning the monitor off, and will just happen as it's being used. Which might compensate for pixel burn-in without as much hassle. Just bear in mind that the word here is "compensation", not "prevention", as it's technically not stopping the burn-in, just, well, compensating for it.

According to recent reports, the company also reportedly highlighted off an ultra-thin 14-inch notebook display prototype using an IJP OLED. I'm not sure how much IJP specifically contributes to the ultra-thinness.

In a recent development, IJP involves printing OLED materials directly onto a substrate rather than having evaporated materials go through a mask. The main benefit is that there's less material wastage, which should, in theory, mean cheaper production and hopefully cheaper costs for the OLED displays made using it. I certainly wouldn't turn my nose up at a 500 Hz OLED that's made much cheaper than it otherwise would be. Roll on 2027, I say.

According to recent reports, my firstest-ever Golden Joystick Awards, which took place last night in London, was marred somewhat by 1) a gin & tonic costing eleven quid and 2) my view of the stage being directly obscured by its own rigging. Nonetheless, I did crane enough to get a good view at the reveal of The Sound of Fury, a musically-minded hack 'n' slash in which a troubled classical musician descends into Hell to save a friend from the Devil.

It's not out until late 2027, and the strength of its monster-battering will of course lay in how it feels in the hand. I like the look of this one, though. While it doesn't appear to be a full-on rhythm action game in the Hi-Fi Rush or Dead as Disco vein, it's clearly trying incorporate our glum hero's virtuosity with both visual and thematic flair: spinning attacks are accentuated by trails of sheet music staves, and at least one move inflicts enemies with uncontrollable bouts of dancing. Weapons also take the form of instruments, the trailer being particularly keen to show grand pianos being powerbombed into demon heads. "You dropped your... keys," I will say, to the demons. Heh heh heh.

Recent findings suggest that also of note is The Sound of Fury's unusual interpretation of Hell, which rather than the usual Biblical/Nordic/Ancient Greek depictions we get in games, is a washed-out mashup of what the Steam page calls "humanity's darkest chapters." Thus, you fight not red-skinned horned imps but gasmasked soldiers and Klu Klux Klansmen, with history-spanning anomalies distorting an otherwise 19th century-flavoured fantasyscape. The laws of time evidently aren't followed here, not least when the protag whips out a Flying V guitar to give the Grim Reaper a different kind of axe wound.

It has been revealed that I can't find much else out about developers and self-publishers Games By Wojtek, with that pluralisation assuming 'they' aren't just one person named Wojtek, but The Sound of Fury looks to be his/their debut game. Hopefully it gets a demo, in due course, so we can try tickling its ivories ourselves.

Tech Report: Paradox boss Frederik Wester stepping down after several tumultuous years for the Cities Skylines and Stellaris publisher

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, paradox Interactive's Frederik Wester has unveiled he's stepping down from the role of CEO after a combined decade and a half leading the firm.
  • In a statement announcing the change in leadership, Paradox said Wester had "decided to step down as CEO to continue focusing on the tech giant's long-term development as a member of the Board." Paradox's current deputy CEO, Mattias Lilja, will take over Wester's role from 4th January 2027.
  • Sources indicate that "I'm truly grateful to all our engaged players and talented colleagues who contribute to outstanding gaming experiences every day," Wester said of his decision.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, paradox Interactive's Frederik Wester has unveiled he's stepping down from the role of CEO after a combined decade and a half leading the firm. The news follows several tumultuous years for the publisher best known for grand strategy games including Stellaris, Europa Universalis, and Crusader Kings 3.

In a statement announcing the change in leadership, Paradox said Wester had "decided to step down as CEO to continue focusing on the tech giant's long-term development as a member of the Board." Paradox's current deputy CEO, Mattias Lilja, will take over Wester's role from 4th January 2027. Wester is to remain in the position until then in order "to ensure an orderly transition".

Sources indicate that "I'm truly grateful to all our engaged players and talented colleagues who contribute to outstanding gaming experiences every day," Wester said of his decision. "They are the ones who made these years amazing. My plan was never to be CEO for life. The goal was to build the foundation before passing the baton on for the next chapter in the manufacturer's journey. Since I returned as CEO, we've streamlined our strategy, rebuilt our pipeline and developed our commercial offering. Mattias has had a central role in laying this foundation, and now is the right time to hand over. Given his experience and vision, he is exceptionally well positioned to take the company to its next level.".

In a recent development, wester has twice served as Paradox CEO since joining the company in 2003. His first stint ran from 2009 to 2018, after which he became Paradox's executive chairman of the board. He returned to the CEO role in 2021, and has overseen a troubled period for the company. This has included the embattled development of Vampire: The Masquerade Bloodlines 2 - which finally released last October after multiple delays, near cancellation, and a switch in developer. Unfortunately the game failed to resonate with critics and audiences, and Paradox announced a 162 percent decline in operating profit earlier this year as a result of its commercial failure.

Wester's most recent watch - which began with an admittance of "inappropriate behaviour" amid a damning report into Paradox's workplace culture - has also seen the high-profile cancellation of Sims competitor Life By You, an indefinite delay for Prison Architect 2 after Paradox parted ways with original developer Double Eleven, and a split with BattleTech studio Harebrained Schemes following the commercial failure of The Lamplighters League. Paradox's Cities Skylines 2 has also been blighted with controversy: after a disastrous launch in 2023, its console release is still yet to emerge, and development is now being handled by a latest studio after Paradox split with former developer Colossal Order last year. In 2004, Wester admitted the publisher had "made the wrong calls in several projects".

Recent findings suggest that despite all this, incoming CEO Mattias Lilja remains buoyant. "Paradox has a unique DNA that has made us one of the greats in deep and engaging strategy and management games," he wrote in a statement announcing his promotion. "Now we’re stepping up the pace: we will make further investments in our core business, push the boundaries of our game design, work even more closely with our loyal players, develop more and better tools and services that benefit both modders and players, and continue to sharpen our ways of working and our organisation, with player value in focus.".

Paradox, does of course, have some promising games on its upcoming slate. Alongside continued work on grand strategy stalwarts like Crusader Kings 3, Europa Universalis 5, and Stellaris, next year sees the release of Lego Skylines, and post-apocalyptic grand strategy game Afterworld is also on the way.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since we're already sharing trailers from non-Geoff awards reveals, here's another: a first in-motion look at Lola's Familiars: Prison of Argnoh, a 2D side-scroller and "lite-vania" that sees its shy witch-in-training making her first summonable friends. Then, borrowing their powers to bust out of a dark fantasy oubliette.

It looks like this'll be a mix of passively familiar-enhanced punching and more active, mayhaps traditionally Metroid-y power upgrades, Lola's ghastly pals looming over her tiny frame when called upon. It's all presented in a hand-drawn, lightly anime-ish style, complete with a story setup straight out of Saturday morning TV – Lola's only stuck in Skullcatraz because of a summoning-gone-wrong that occurred in pursuit of her school's unlikely Ofsted-compliant 'familiar contest'. I've attended school several times, and will attest that non-sporting contests, which students remain unaware of until seeing a poster for them, do not exist outside of childrens' television*.

According to recent reports, this doesn't seem to be kid fodder, though. Lola's a bean but the familiars, and the prison's other denizens, are growling towers of jaws and decaying flesh. Developers Caracal Games are promising they'll star in a "heartfelt and emotionally resonant story about growth," to balance out the grimness, though I'm less clear on a following blurb point that declares it a "lite-vania," into which you'll "dive into exploration, trial-and-error and platforming, without feeling frustrated." While this might just be an attempt to assuage fears that this'll a Hollow Knight- or Nine Sols-style controller-thrower, I do wonder how one goes light on 'vania. Maybe some of the ability gates open if you just ask them nicely?

In a recent development, that aside, I'm already quite charmed by Lola's Familiars, especially the designs of its bag-eyed wallflower of a heroine and her contrastingly hench minions. Release date is TBC, but the Steam page is up.

*Granted, no TV example was ever as egregiously misleading as Jack Black vehicle School of Rock, which convinced me - then a barely-pubescent aspiring bassist - that winning a local Battle of the Bands would pay out thousands in cash, as opposed to the drinks rounds and packs of guitar strings I'd end up competing for a few years later.

Recent findings suggest that valve CEO and co-founder Gabe Newell has been under fire lately, pretty much entirely from Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, but the self-described "father of Lovecraftian gaming" has leapt to his defense. Without Newell, argues Doom and Quake veteran Sandy Petersen, PC gamers would have nothing to protect them from storefronts run by mega corporations.

"I know Gabe Newell. We have chatted at some length. I know numerous men who worked for him as well," writes Petersen on Twitter. "I am sure that there must be some disgruntled ex-employees out there but everyone I know who has dealt with him respects and admires him.

Sources indicate that "And with Steam he is literally guarding the gates of Hell - preserving all gamers from the horrors of what would happen if parasites like Disney, EA, or MicroSoft became the providers ... May he live forever.".

Recent findings suggest that I know Gabe Newell. We have chatted at some length. I know numerous men who worked for him as well. I am sure that there must be some disgruntled ex-employees out there but everyone I know who has dealt with him respects and admires him. And with Steam he is literally guarding the gates of Hell - preserving all gamers from the horrors of what would happen if parasites like Disney, EA, or MicroSoft became the providers. May he live forever.November 16, 2026.

Sources indicate that of course, Valve itself is a big corporation, but not nearly on the same level as Microsoft, Disney, or EA, and it's also a historically consumer-friendly one compared to other tech giants. Since I mentioned Sweeney, I'll use the example of Steam's mandatory AI disclosure, which requires developers to inform Steam users if there's any AI-generated content in their games. Sweeney has repeatedly railed against this in his full-throated embrace of AI in games, but Valve has shown no indication that it's considering walking back that policy even after a Steam Next Fest that was overrun by AI-generated games. Valve is far from perfect, but if you're gonna have one manufacturer all-but monopolizing the PC market, you could do far worse.

Petersen isn't the only one vouching for Newell. A recent video tour of Newell's ridiculous yacht, the Leviathan, revealed an endearing fact about the famously eccentric billionaire: he actually hangs out and eats with the crew on-board the vessel, proving that not every rich person treats regular people like insects.

Valve "played capitalism so well they broke it" and now Steam can never be replaced, former Epic dev says: "I don't think this is fixable".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Well folks, it's official: Grand Theft Auto 6 reviews are out, and it's presently tied with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (N64) as the highest-rated game ever on Metacritic.

There may yet be time for things to change as more reviews trickle in, but at the time of writing, GTA 6 is sitting at a remarkable 99 on the aggregate website, based on a total of 134 reviews.

Ocarina of Time, meanwhile, has a mere 22 critic reviews making up that lofty 99 average (it was a different time, man), so one could argue that GTA 6's result is probably more impressive – especially in an age in which it's getting harder and harder to make such an impact.

Our pals over at Push Square were emphatic in their praise, calling GTA 6 "the greatest open world game" in their 10/10 review. Meanwhile, our other pals over at Pure Xbox also gave it 10/10, stating "Rockstar Games has crafted the most incredible open world I've ever experienced in a video game, packed with so much detail that I'll want to continue exploring it for months and likely years to come".

Industry observers note that there are 10s all over the damn place, with the only outliers awarding it 9s or 90s at the lowest. It's pretty unprecedented stuff.

We'll keep an eye on things and upgrade this article if GTA 6 does happen to slip below Ocarina of Time. Elsewhere, the latter's Switch 2 remake also released to almost universal acclaim earlier this month. Critic reviews on Metacritic average out at 96, while it also boasts the highest user review score of all time at 9.6.

It has been revealed that what do you make of GTA 6's Metacritic score at the moment? Are you excited to play it for yourself? Let us know with a comment down below.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Developer FromSoftware has revealed that online multiplayer servers for Dark Souls 2 and 3 are back online following a nearly two-week outage.

Recent findings suggest that fromSoftware temporarily disabled multiplayer on 30th October, citing what it called "a server glitch". Some speculated this could be related to the recently discovered PHP security bug, which impacted a number of other games.

Sources indicate that fromSoftware never specified the exact glitch impacting its servers, and today's statement is equally vague. "Regarding the temporary suspension of the game server for Dark Souls 2, and Dark Souls 3, the investigation has been completed and the fix has been applied. The game server and online features are now restored," a notice on Dark Souls' official site reads.

"We sincerely apologise for the inconvenience caused, and thank you for your patience and understanding.".

Online servers do more in FromSoftware games than simply facilitating co-op and PvP; they're also responsible for handling messages players leave for each other in-game, as well as the ghostly representations of players who just went through the same area, helping the Dark Souls series' forlorn worlds feel a little less solitary.

It has been revealed that this isn't the first time Dark Souls servers have gone offline, either. In 2022, servers for all three games went offline due to a vulnerability that allowed malicious code to run on them. In that instance, it took FromSoftware three months to bring servers back online for some games, and as many as nine months for others.

In other FromSoftware news, the studio recently announced - following months of speculation - it's officially delaying the Switch 2-exclusive The Duskbloods to sometime in 2027.

Recent findings suggest that I feel like one thing I only sort of miss from my youth, viewed through the lenses of those rose tinted goggles, is the established intellectual property game that just copies the formula of another, successful game. Obviously there are plenty of genres that are trendy to imitate, but how often do you see something that's just sort of "thing you know slapped on top of game you know?" Perhaps that's a tad mean, but I do genuinely have a fondness for such games, so I'm quite pleased by the announcement of Conan: The Black Pyramid, an action roguelite RPG that so clearly went to Supergiant Games' School of Hades you have to admire the boldness just a little bit.

In a recent development, conan: The Black Pyramid puts you in the hotseat as the titular barbarian, of course, but also as other characters from the series like Solomon Kane, Dark Agnes, and apparently, more! So, immediately, a notable enough difference from Hades, and one that seems like a neat take. As one of them you then "Descend into eldritch chambers of the Black Pyramid, a mysterious and dangerous place that defies the logic of space and time. Confront the shadows of the champions themselves and piece together the dark secrets of their past.".

Where it is similar to Hades lies in the fact that the titular triangle changes in form each time you go in it, and of course there are different abilities and buffs to pick up along the way to aid you in your quest. Each character has their own combination of weapons and abilities, so it does sound like you can mix it up quite nicely. There is, also, 2-player online co-op (sorry to the couch lovers, I suppose), adding to the ways it differs and making it a tad more friendly for those that have exactly one friend who also loves Conan.

Overall, seems like a fresh enough take on Hades while still trying to find some amount of its own identity. And hey, Hades is great, so I'm never upset about having a little bit more of that kind of game. No release date attached to Conan: The Black Pyramid just yet, but it is planned to arrive sometime in 2027. You can check it out on Steam here.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sam Altman, the CEO of OpenAI, got in hot water late last month when he said, "From a global allocation perspective, actually it’s quite terrible to have everyone have a bunch of the world’s limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer, and be used 5% of the time".
  • Altman notes, "I want to be clear, I want people to have a lot of RAM.
  • Altman says his comment was "misinterpreted, but there is a true part of it".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sam Altman, the CEO of OpenAI, got in hot water late last month when he said, "From a global allocation perspective, actually it’s quite terrible to have everyone have a bunch of the world’s limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer, and be used 5% of the time". He has since gone on to say he wants everyone to have RAM, actually, and in a conversation with Semafor, he has elaborated on what he claims he actually means (via The Verge).

Altman notes, "I want to be clear, I want people to have a lot of RAM. I think everybody should buy a lot of RAM, be able to buy a lot of RAM for their own computer. I think this is good. I think the home tinkering is great.".

So why the discrepancy? Altman says his comment was "misinterpreted, but there is a true part of it". He argues that the optimal way to use memory is to share it (in this case, he seems to be referring to the use of AI in home rigs), and "have it working 100% of the time. Rather than, like, sometimes off in someone's Edge device.".

According to recent reports, so I guess if we all share RAM, we get more at the end of the day. I'll wait for OpenAI to share its memory with me, and then I might do the same.

Sources indicate that altman points out that he got in more trouble a few years ago for saying there would be "a huge squeeze on memory". He then notes that many didn't believe it would be such a worry, and "we have seen DRAM prices, I don't know exactly, but maybe they went up like 5x, 7x or something like that. I think it would be much better if the world just had a lot of memory.".

AI server demand is the biggest cause of the current memory crisis, so in a way it's sort of like driving down the road at 100 mph with an air horn, then blaming the post you hit with your car because you warned it you were driving fast.

Industry observers note that in a time when it's a real struggle to pick up memory, it reads as particularly tone deaf for one of the leading causes of that supply constraint to blame the manufacturers. That's before mentioning how long it might take to ramp up memory production, and how risky building too fast can be.

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products.

Altman mused on a few more things in his chat with Semafor. When asked if Nvidia should bring back ex CEO Jensen Huang, Altman claims "it's hard to imagine the AI revolution without Jensen" but also says he doesn't think he knows enough to say if he should come back.

When asked about AI scepticism from investors, Altman claims, "I think there's a lot of scepticism from journalists. Investors seem to be pretty bullish on AI". Well, he's got me pegged.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S officially celebrated their sixth anniversaries back on November 10th, and to mark the occasion, Niko Partners analyst Daniel Ahmad has been looking into a whole bunch of sales estimates.

In a post over on social media, Ahmad estimated that the Series X and S are now at a combined 38 million sales worldwide, and then compared that figure to loads of other consoles that we've seen throughout the years.

The comparison is specifically referencing the sales of each console after six years on the market, so when the Xbox 360 is referenced at 60 million sales, for example, it still racked up another 20+ million until it was discontinued.

According to recent reports, as you can see, it doesn't make for great reading overall. Sony has shipped a lot more PS5 consoles than Microsoft has Xbox consoles throughout this generation, and even compared to past Xbox systems, the Series X and S have struggled to keep pace. That said, the original Xbox only racked up around 25m sales, so that one's been beaten at least.

Ahmad also points out that "console players are monetizing at levels significantly higher than any prior gen", so even though hardware sales have been poor for Xbox, content and services revenue has grown massively in recent years.

In a recent development, people will point to this kind of stuff as evidence that Xbox is "failing", but Microsoft is much more interested in the content and services side of things, and that's been a much bigger success for them since the Xbox Series X and S first launched. With Project Helix around the corner though, they'll still hope they can attract a bigger piece of the pie in the hardware space, although that'll be a very tough ask amidst an ongoing component crisis.

What's your takeaway here? Let us know your thoughts down in the comments section below.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Even as a longtime fan of SCS Software's line of truck simulators, I still have a little difficulty believing just how popular they've remained over the past decade. American Truck Simulator just hit a fresh concurrent player record in September thanks to a fresh bit of DLC that lets you escape the trucking grind, and now Euro Truck Simulator 2 has done the same on a much more impressive scale.

Recent findings suggest that on November 12, the Coaches DLC launched for Euro Truck Simulator 2. For my fellow Americans, you can translate "coaches" to "buses" – this is an expansion all about getting behind the wheel of a public transportation vehicle, picking up passengers, and taking them on long-distance trips across Europe. Like with American Truck Simulator's Road Trip DLC, it offers a whole newly introduced way to explore a now-massive map, and fans have been playing it in droves.

It has been revealed that euro Truck Simulator 2 reached a newly introduced all-time Steam concurrent player record of 101,783 on November 15, as SteamDB shows. That's a massive jump over the previous record of 73,887, set back in February, and genuinely incredible for a game that was first released in 2012.

According to recent reports, 14 years on Steam, with a dedicated community that's passionate, creative & has always supported us 🙏 We've smashed our record (again!) today with 101,000+ concurrent players on Steam! Thank you, everyone! ❤️ We're excited for the future of Euro Truck Simulator 2 🚛🚌 https://t.co/IYfE2x4XM5November 15, 2026.

It has been revealed that "14 years on Steam, with a dedicated community that's passionate, creative & has always supported us," community manager Alex Blackman enthuses in a tweet. "We've smashed our record (again!) today with 101,000+ concurrent players on Steam! Thank you, everyone!".

In a recent development, in fact, Blackman himself might offer a good example of just how dedicated that community is. He founded TruckersFM, an online radio station built for truck sim players and run by a dedicated team of volunteer DJs. While Blackman has moved to work for SCS itself, TruckersFM is still going strong over a decade after it was founded. Who knows what that community will look like in another decade's time?

So what does the future hold? Let the speculation begin!

💡 Key Takeaways
  • CD Projekt Red has revealed that it used - and is using - generative AI technology to treat and alter the voice of the Polish actor who portrayed Geralt of Rivia in upcoming Witcher 3 expansion Songs of the Past.
  • In a recent development, the actor, Jacek Rozenek, has portrayed Geralt of Rivia in all the major Witcher games, meaning his voice has become as synonymous with the role in Poland as Doug Cockle's has for people playing in English.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

CD Projekt Red has revealed that it used - and is using - generative AI technology to treat and alter the voice of the Polish actor who portrayed Geralt of Rivia in upcoming Witcher 3 expansion Songs of the Past.

In a recent development, the actor, Jacek Rozenek, has portrayed Geralt of Rivia in all the major Witcher games, meaning his voice has become as synonymous with the role in Poland as Doug Cockle's has for people playing in English. But Rozenek suffered a severe stroke in 2019 that left him temporarily unable to speak, and when he was able to talk and perform again, the tonality and quality of his voice had changed.

Industry observers note that it's for these reasons that CD Projekt Red - with Rozenek's consent - employed the help of a company called Respeecher to alter the lines he recorded for The Witcher 3's Songs of the Past expansion using generative-AI technology. As confirmed to Game File, an AI trained on Rozenek's previous Witcher work is retreating his recordings to make them sound more like the Geralt you hear elsewhere in The Witcher 3.

"The point is that this voice should be as close as possible to my voice from 12 years ago," Jacek Rozenek explained. "I have great trust ... for the creators of this game.".

Game File heard both treated and untreated recordings of Rozenek's Songs of the Past work, and reported a "significant" difference between them. Rozenek's untreated voice was apparently "deep and gravelly" and "noticeably rougher than his recordings for the original game". But treated, the voice was "far smoother and sounds younger", and closer to the original Witcher 3 Geralt recordings.

This isn't the first time CD Projekt Red has used generative AI for voice recordings in one of its games. The studio worked with Respeecher in 2023 to produce newly introduced voiceover lines for Cyberpunk 2077 expansion Phantom Liberty. Viktor Vektor actor Miłogost "Miłek" Reczek passed away in 2021, after the original game was released, and CD Projekt Red didn't want to recast the role. Reczek's sons apparently gave their blessing for their father's voice to be artificially generated.

"I do think this is one of those ways where you can use AI ethically with consent and also to do something good," CD Projekt Red localisation producer Mikołaj Szwed told Game File, referring to the Rozenek recordings.

Industry observers note that "For future projects, when we consider Geralt is becoming older and has a deeper voice, this is not a problem for us at all. It's more about this specific situation here, where we have both the voice from 12 years ago and from now next to each other, which could kind of take people out of the experience and feel that there is this difference.".

According to recent reports, the third Witcher 3 expansion, Songs of the Past, releases at some point next year, an unprecedented 12 years after the original game debuted. It adds an entirely upcoming region, Letten, and centres its main story around Geralt's missing bardic bestie Dandelion, whose family lives there.

In preparation for the expansion, a remastered version of The Witcher 3 was released a couple of months ago, overhauling the old role-playing adventure and bringing its baseline presentation more in line with what we'd expect from a modern game; it also overhauled some animations and enemy behaviours and reworked skill trees. For that reason, old-gen consoles PS4 and Xbox One won't receive the Songs of the Past expansion, despite The Witcher 3 being available on them.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We've spent most of 2026 seeing the consequences of other developers trying to get the hell out of GTA 6's way – which, for most of us players, has meant a whole lot of fresh games to play in September and October and very few to choose from in November. One of the few brave enough to take on GTA 6 head-to-head is Binding of Isaac developer Edmund McMillen, and he's not too worried about going up against the titan.

It has been revealed that the Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ is a free DLC expansion that launched on PC back in 2024, and is now coming to consoles on November 19, the same day that GTA 6 launches. Apparently, this was the idea of publisher Nicalis, and McMillen agreed that it would, if nothing else, be pretty funny, as he tells Eurogamer.

"There's a possibility [Repentance+'s release date] wasn't that stupid an idea," McMillen indicates, "and if it was a stupid idea, it's a funny stupid idea." But he does have experience with having a game's thunder stolen by a much bigger competitor, as was the case when he launched strategy roguelike Mewgenics just a few weeks ahead of roguelike deckbuilder Splay the Spire 2 earlier this year.

"My heart says it doesn't matter, but my brain has shown me it does," he says. "When Mewgenics came out it blew up; we went past two million sales almost right off the bat. It was such a blasting, skyrocketing thing for like three weeks. Then Slay the Spire 2 came out, and it sucked everybody out. The same players who liked Mewgenics, they were Slay The Spire players. So they all went woosh and right over.".

Clearly, it's a much different prospect with Binding of Isaac DLC and GTA 6 – a cult roguelike with a devoted audience versus the biggest entertainment launch in, well, maybe ever. That's very different from two hot upcoming roguelikes trading the same group of genre enthusiasts back and forth, and McMillen is hopeful, as many industry analysts are, that GTA 6 could help get people buying and playing console games again.

It has been revealed that "Logically, there's a record number of people who are going to be on the console the game is on at launch [because of GTA 6]," McMillen says. "They might be like me, play [GTA 6] for a while, and say, 'Okay, I have a console with one game, what am I going to play next?' Then, you know, a rising tide will raise all ships. I think Grand Theft Auto will bring people back to consoles, because consoles are abysmal right now. Sales are bad and no one is playing anything.".

These are the best roguelike games you can play today.

He's been covering games (with occasional dalliances in the worlds of anime and pro wrestling) since 2015, first as a freelancer, then as a news writer at PCGamesN for nearly five years. His love for games was sparked somewhere between Metal Gear Solid 2 and Knights of the Old Republic, and these days you can usually find him splitting his entertainment time between retro gaming, the latest major action-adventure title, or a long haul in American Truck Simulator.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia's founder and CEO Jensen Huang has resigned from his position as leader of one of the most valuable companies in the world.
  • After days mired in controversy, which began amid reports of Huang's alleged affair with a Chinese spy, Nvidia has unveiled Huang's resignation as company president, chief executive officer, and board member, effective immediately.
  • According to recent reports, "Colette has helped lead Nvidia through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position," Harvey Jones, chair of Nvidia's board of directors wrote in a statement accompanying the news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia's founder and CEO Jensen Huang has resigned from his position as leader of one of the most valuable companies in the world.

After days mired in controversy, which began amid reports of Huang's alleged affair with a Chinese spy, Nvidia has unveiled Huang's resignation as company president, chief executive officer, and board member, effective immediately. Finance chief Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO and will remain in the position until a permanent CEO is chosen.

According to recent reports, "Colette has helped lead Nvidia through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position," Harvey Jones, chair of Nvidia's board of directors wrote in a statement accompanying the news. "She is supported by an experienced leadership team that has been instrumental in executing Nvidia's strategy and advancing its technology roadmap. The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the tech giant's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption.".

Kress, in the same announcement, indicates she intends to build on the foundation laid by Huang over the past 33 years, and "continue advancing the work that has made Nvidia a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead." Perhaps unsurprisingly, there's no mention of gaming graphics cards in there.

Nvidia's announcement ends by thanking Huang for his time at the company: "Jensen’s contributions to Nvidia are profound. Nvidia is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry.".

According to recent reports, nvidia's board met on Wednesday to decide whether to remove Huang amid allegations he had participated in a second affair, this time with a subordinate, following reports of his alleged affair with a Chinese spy. That initial incident prompted a tech giant-wide apology from Huang and an independent investigation exploring whether he'd been the target of a "foreign intelligence effort".

According to recent reports, nvidia will likely remain under increased scrutiny moving forward. There are particular concerns around the manufacturer's chips being imported to China despite trade bans.

Is there a character not originally from a video game that has more games than Barbie? Maybe! I don't want to do any maths right now, but there aren't many that could touch her on sheer numbers. She's had all sorts of digital adventures, her games having a huge influence on the world of 'girl games'. As complicatedly gendered that may now be, the significance can't be understated, and as of today you can have a romp through a nice portion of that history in Barbie Rewind, a compilation of almost two decades worth of games all wrapped up in a nice little decorating game.

The latest release from Digital Eclipse, aficionados of digital multi-pack games like Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration and last year's Mortal Kombat: Legacy Kollection, Barbie Rewind has a total of 16 games from across the doll's video game history. Starting all the way back in 1991 with Barbie for the original NES, it jumps around to the Game Boy Color with Barbie: Pet Rescue, to the SNES with Barbie: Vacation Adventure. That last one's crucial because it's actually an unreleased game, making it quite a neat addition to the package.

Sources indicate that beyond that, there's the customizable DreamHouse, where you get a whole bunch of furniture to deck it out with. Nothing overly complicated here, it's just a thematically appropriate appendage that helps to recreate the feeling of playing with a doll house in pixel art form. Expect familiar faces like Ken, Teresa and Christie to pop up here and there as well. You'll also find a digital lookbook where you can "flip through the pages of Barbie history.".

In a recent development, perhaps slightly disappointingly you won't find a number of beloved Barbie games like Barbie: Secret Agent or Barbie Horse Adventures: Mystery Ride. A lot of the games in this package are the 2D, pixel art entries, so that was probably meant to be the focus here. Hopefully someone will part those 3D releases somewhere down the line! In any case, if you fancy a trip down memory lane, you can pick up Barbie Rewind on Steam now.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

More indie developers say they've been forced to delay the impending release of their games as a result of Steam's growing approvals backlog - a relatively recent problem that's believed to stem from an influx of AI slop on the platform.

In a recent development, earlier this month, developers began complaining about delays to Valve's approval process, which was extending the time it took to get their games published on Steam. Valve responded, explaining approval times could now take up to 12 days, due to the number of submissions it was having to re-review. One week on, the situation doesn't seem to have improved.

New turn-based tower defence game Australia Did It: End-of-the-World Railway Defense Business, co-developed by acclaimed indie designer Rami Ismail and Aesthetician Labs, was previously set for release on 10th November. Unfortunately, the game has now been delayed while the wait continues for Valve to review the latest build.

Industry observers note that "We're still waiting for Steam to give us the final greenlight and finish their build review process," publisher Mystic Forge wrote on the Steam forums. "We have been stuck waiting for it for a few weeks now and unfortunately we just don't know when they will get around to reviewing it at this point.".

Speaking to Eurogamer, Ismail added that Australia Did It has been in Steam's approval queue for much longer than he's used to: "We've been in the queue since 20th October, failed over a minor controller input matter on 5th November (which we resolved the same day), and we've been waiting again since with no meaningful response from Valve despite follow-ups.".

"I'm used to hold-and-wait patterns on console," Ismail continued, "but Steam has historically been much more snappy - 10-14 days pre-launch was usually enough to fail twice and still ship on time," he added.

It has been revealed that amazing Slot Survivor (A.S.S.), the debut title from TwoMenGames, is facing similar issues, and has had to retract its release date announcement after being stuck in Steam's approval queue. Amazing Slot Survivor, which adds a slot machine spin to the bullet heaven auto-shooting genre, was initially set for release on 13th November.

Industry observers note that "Steam's review process for the release is taking longer than we expected," TwoMenGames wrote in a message on Steam. "We know many of you have been counting on the schedule we declared earlier, and we are very sorry to bring you this [postponement] news instead of the good news you were hoping for." Amazing Slot Survivor's demo, which was previously set to disappear with the game's full release, has returned to Steam until the developer reveals a new launch date.

These are far from the only examples, and a cursory look on social media reveals many more indie games are affected by the problem, including the likes of Bottled by Bears, and Food Devils.

Industry observers note that valve recently attempted to address the delays its facing by introducing stricter submission guidelines designed to stop the lowest-effort games, such as those vibe-coded entirely with gen-AI, from joining its approval queue. However, Ismail doesn't think that's good enough.

"I am concerned that Valve trying to avoid taking a political position on AI is forcing them into choices that will inevitably be worse for developers," he told Eurogamer. "If sloppers can submit several game clones a day through automated systems, the only way for Valve to stem the tide of games damaging genuine developers' work is to put constraints on game distribution, increase fees, or make the process more complicated.

"In the 'open market' Valve seems to so adore, they're going to be the ones carrying the costs for moderation, so I don't think they'll like the open market on this - but there's no outcome of this that allows Valve neutrality on AI and not do things that will ultimately make life worse for genuine developers," he added.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Spoilers ahead for the most recent episode of The Gilded Age.

According to recent reports, shortly after its debut, Julian Fellowes' The Gilded Age joined the ranks of HBO shows that got the world talking. The show's fourth season began a few weeks ago on the network (and streaming with a HBO Max subscription), and there have already been a number of memorable moments. The third episode featured Peggy's marriage to Dr. William Kirkland, and Audra McDonald as well as executive producer Erica Armstrong Dunbar spoke about the importance of having the newlyweds jump the broom onscreen.

Sources indicate that while The Gilded Age fans are concerned over Marian and Larry, Peggy and William have officially tied the knot. In a conversation with People, McDonald spoke said "it meant everything" for the series to show the latest pair jumping the broom onscreen, highlighting similar opinions to her character Dorothy. In the Broadway legend's words:.

We’re honoring those traditions. We’re celebrating those traditions. We are shouting into the world who we are. I think that’s why it was crucial to Dorothy and Arthur [John Douglas Thompson], and especially because that was their broom, the one that they jumped over.

For those unfamiliar, jumping the broom is a wedding ceremony that goes back antebellum period in the United States. While enslaved people couldn't legally get married, couples would jump over a broom together to symbolize their union. It's remained a tradition for Black Americans in the years that followed, continuing to this day.

Jumping the broom became a point of contention leading up to Peggy's wedding, with her mother-in-law Elizabeth Kirkland (Phylicia Rashad) protesting its place in high society. Later in the same interview, Audra McDonald spoke more about why Dorothy and the entire Scott family was so passionate about it being included in the wedding ceremony, offering:.

[It meant that] our family is going to continue. That’s another thing. We didn’t know about the Scotts, how we were going to make it, especially with all the trauma that they went through, that we’re going to continue as a unified family. Now we have the possibility of future generations.

It has been revealed that indeed, the Scott family has come a long way since Season 1 of The Gilded Age. Despite trauma and complications, Peggy and her parents have found their way back to each other throughout the last three seasons. It was actually the same broom that Dorothy and Arthur jumped over before they were able to legally marry, making Peggy's use of the ceremony a full circle moment for the entire family.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that but it's not that too much time behind the computer is keeping WoW players on the other side of the globe away from their precious Vitamin D.
  • World of Warcraft: Forever, if you didn't already known, has a lovely in-game day/night cycle that aligns with your server clock rather than your local time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that world of Warcraft: Forever players are having a blast in the fresh MMO, but not everyone is basking in the rays of its successful launch. Players located in Australia, New Zealand, and other Oceania countries are having a bit of a sunlight problem.

It has been revealed that but it's not that too much time behind the computer is keeping WoW players on the other side of the globe away from their precious Vitamin D. Rather, it's in-game sunlight that's scarce for our Oceania friends.

World of Warcraft: Forever, if you didn't already known, has a lovely in-game day/night cycle that aligns with your server clock rather than your local time. So, for a British player, the server time is one hour ahead of GMT. That means if I play during the day I see the sun hanging over Azeroth, and if I do a late night MMO session it's replaced by the moon.

Sources indicate that however, while Oceania players can access a data centre in Australia that allows for a solid connection to WoW, they still share the same mega-servers with North Americans. That mega-server is aligned with North American time, differing drastically from Oceania time zones. In other words, for World of Warcraft: Forever players in Oceania, day is night and night is day. And they've had enough!

According to recent reports, reddit user Playful_Artichoke981 has been at the forefront of requests asking Blizzard to address the problem , though they're far from alone. Currently, Oceania players see full daylight in-game from around midnight to 6am in the morning, which obviously is far from normal gaming hours for the majority of players in the region.

"We don't hate the nighttime. We just want variety," writes Playful_Artichoke981. "We don't want to have to compromise our sleep schedules to experience this game in all its glory." Another user, cuddlegoop, echoes the sentiment: "I am totally fine with my day/night changing when I join an NA party. Just let me see the sun! I was up late last night and the view over the bay at Shadowfan Keep in the dawn was so beautiful I want to see stuff like that more often.".

Eurogamer has contacted Blizzard to ask if it has plans to address the issue, but we've not received a response at the time of writing.

It has been revealed that world of Warcraft: Forever is proving exceptionally popular, breaking records as the biggest launch in the series' history. And based on what I've played this week, it's looking to be a brilliant MMO that's well worth jumping into, if you have the time.

According to recent reports, I often find it quite dull that the main takeaway far too many people have taken from Dark Souls, aside from thinking that the most interesting thing is its combat, is that it's all so bloomin' grimdark. I'm not saying I need sunshine and rainbows, I'd just like a vibe that's even remotely trying to be different from FromSoftware's seminal work. And so! I am quite pleased to discover MycoRelic, a Soulslike that pits you as a robot that covers its body in mushroom parts that offer elemental powers.

It has been revealed that mycoRelic, from the offset, has this low-poly style that almost reminds me of oldschool RuneScape in a way I clown with quite promptly. The game looks good! The vibes look odd and, thankfully, not particularly derivative of medieval aesthetics. But while I am vibes-first when it comes to games, a Soulslike does live and die by its systems, and the systems here sound quite intriguing.

Recent findings suggest that for starters, there are no classes to speak of, just various weapons with their own moves and stats, and armour that "suits your playstyle and aesthetic." Huzzah! A game that understands one of the best bits of Dark Souls is dressing up. When you start out, you just have a "decrepit, moldy frame," but over time you can replace parts of it to improve your health, stamina, frame integrity, and the "potency of your fungal magic." Mycellic music to my ears.

Different fungi have different powers, and can be combined to create latest effects, or used in a multitude of ways; healing water can restore your friends or put out a fire for example. And oh, yes, there's co-op too, though I don't know if it's the friction-heavy Dark Souls kind or the seamless, hassle-free kind. On top of all this you've got an air-dash and can glide too, offering up some tasty platforming potential not typically found in the genre. I like it! And it just came out in 1.0 after a period of early access. If you fancy giving it a go, there's still a demo on Steam, or you can just pick up the full thing.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that I don't remember much about my coverage from Steam Next Fest this past June, but I remember my time playing the demo for Tanuki: Pon's Summer very vividly. I mean, how could I forget? I rail-grinded around an adorable Japanese town as a potbellied Tanuki on a BMX bike doing tricks in the air while delivering packages for residents. The little demo that could is now a full-fledged game with "Very Positive" Steam reviews, and although it pains me to say it probably won't take home any Game of the Year awards in December, it deserves its time in the spotlight even with an incredibly unfortunate release right smack-dab between Zelda: Ocarina of Time's remake and GTA 6. Naturally, its director agrees.

Talking to GamesIndustry.biz, Denkiworks co-founder and game director Liam Edwards acknowledges the disadvantages of releasing a niche indie game in-between two of the biggest games of the year, one of which is considered to be the largest entertainment product ever made in terms of scope and budget. "What I don't think we could have accounted for was Nintendo shadow-dropping the release of Ocarina of Time [on November 5]," says Edwards. "There's probably a fair bit more of an overlap with Switch 2 Zelda players for Tanuki than there would be for GTA 6.".

It has been revealed that still, the team at Denkiworks is taking it all in stride, basking calmly in Zelda and GTA's shadow, and hoping Tanuki will get caught in our collective headlights at some point. He argues that Tanuki: Pon's Summer could be the "lovely little underdog" waiting for you when you're doing playing the two November behemoths.

"I don't think you can account for what others do even in such a crazy period," he says. "You know your game's strengths best, and you have to continue to promote it as such. We've worked with the publishing team [Critical Reflex] to find places that Pon would shine and have seen a lot of success with that.

"Hopefully, in the long term, word-of-mouth and the fact that it's been well-received means a long tail; when players are done with Zelda and GTA 6, they'll be looking for what's next and might think, 'Oh, yeah! There was that BMXing Tanuki game!'".

Sources indicate that I know I will, Edwards. I know I will.

Tanuki: Pon's Summer is out now on PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo Switch 1 and 2, and PC.

Hardware Review: Nacon Revolution 5 Unlimited - Solid Xbox-Style PS5 Controller Undercuts Its Competition

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1440 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pushsquare

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that for the last month, I’ve been levelling up my game with the Nacon Revolution 5 Unlimited, a hefty pro controller for PS5.
  • The NACON Revolution 5 Unlimited is a big old pro controller, compatible with both PS5 and PC.
  • It features TMR thumbsticks, eradicating the worry of stick drift, along with swappable thumbstick tips and varying weights to fit in the grips of the controller, so you can customise the feel of the controller to your liking.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that for the last month, I’ve been levelling up my game with the Nacon Revolution 5 Unlimited, a hefty pro controller for PS5. With a myriad of customisable features, including trigger travel length and even its weight, I’m going to break down whether this controller is worth your time.

The NACON Revolution 5 Unlimited is a big old pro controller, compatible with both PS5 and PC. It connects to PS5 via a dongle, can also connect wirelessly, offering 2.4Ghz connection for either, and offers Bluetooth connectivity too.

It features TMR thumbsticks, eradicating the worry of stick drift, along with swappable thumbstick tips and varying weights to fit in the grips of the controller, so you can customise the feel of the controller to your liking.

The substantial headliner here is a screen display in the centre of the controller, which allows access to simple customising menus without the need for an additional app — but we'll get into that later.

This Nacon Revolution 5 Unlimited will set you back £179.90/$229.90, actually making it one of the cheaper options in the pro controller market.

The NACON Revolution 5 Unlimited, which I’m just going to call the Rev5 from now on, comes in a rugged, hardshell case, with NACON branding embossed on the front.

Inside, the controller, of course, along with a collection of switchable thumbsticks, a D-Pad alternative, and weights which can be placed on the inside of the controller, a braided USB-A to C cable, the dongle, and the charging base.

The form factor is easily one of my favourite things about the Rev5. This is a pretty large, meaty controller, which, personally, I really like. It fills the hands, and immediately, all of the buttons feel like they are in naturally reachable places – something that wasn’t the case with the SCUF Omega, in my opinion.

Recent findings suggest that your eye will immediately be drawn to this little screen in the middle, and we’ll get to some of its features in a minute, but it definitely gives the Rev5 a premium look. The grips of the controller offer a ribbed rubber coating with a sleek black finish. The thumbsticks, d-pad, and triggers all have textured finishes, giving each a nice firm feel. There’s a satisfying clicky feel to the face buttons and back paddles, which are naturally placed where my fingers wrap around the back of the controller.

I love the triggers on this thing, which remind me of the Xbox controllers, actually. They have a nice smooth travel for the longer setting, but can also be switched to a mouse-like click, with a toggle on the back. I have to say, these are some of my favourite trigger length toggles that I’ve used on a pro controller. They are so easy to access and customise, without the need for longer nails to pick at them.

My only real complaints about the design are that the finish does make the controller a victim to smudges and smears, and the substitute button for the touchpad is a little small, which can be a pain if you want to quickly check leaderboards, for example.

It has been revealed that connecting this thing to the PS5 is a right doddle. You can use it wired with the braided cable, but most of my use was with the dongle.

According to recent reports, what I really liked about this dongle is that it could be used whilst plugged into the back of the charging base, with a USB-A to C cable connecting to the PS5, meaning you can connect and charge the Rev5 with the use of just one USB-A port. However, if you're on the go, you can also just plug the dongle straight into the PS5, without the need for the charging base.

Industry observers note that annoyingly, however, you aren’t able to turn the PS5 on with this controller. You have to manually turn it on, then connect the Rev5, regardless of whether you are connecting wirelessly or wired.

Then there is that screen, which is really cool, but it did take me a moment to get my head around. A customise button on the top of the controller halts all inputs to the console and lets you navigate a simple menu system.

Here you can customise things like thumbstick dead zones, audio and mic input (if you’re using a wired headset), and customise each of the six additional buttons around the controller.

You’re then able to make four custom profiles, which you can switch between with a tap of the Profile button on the back of the controller. It’s not quite DualSense Edge levels of ease, but it is great.

If a little screen menu isn’t cutting it for you, there is also still the option to download the Nacon app and customise more intensely from there.

Industry observers note that then there is the physical customisation. You are able to switch out thumbsticks, the D-pad, and apply additional weights in the grips of the controllers. All of this is incredibly accessible, as there are no tools required. You can just pull one thing off and replace it with another. The only thing I had a bit of struggle getting off was the smaller variation of the d-pad.

Recent findings suggest that honestly, I think the Rev5 feels great. Once you have a profile that suits you, this thing is just moulded to the hand, with each of its additional paddles easily within reach, and its physical customisation options making it feel tailor-made to you.

Industry observers note that I love the travel of the trigger if going for long triggers, but it features a really satisfying mouse-click if you customise it to short triggers too. The TMR sticks do have that weightless feel that's typical for thumbstick utilising Hall Effect tech, but I adjusted to it quite quickly.

According to recent reports, the easy profile swapping and customisation on the actual controller, and the feel in the hand, meant I was more inclined than ever to just use this thing for regular games, not just those competitive titles like The Finals or Modern Warfare 4. I actually played most of Zero Parades using this controller, just because it was comfortable to use, despite not using a single customisation aspect.

There is a pretty big flaw, however, regarding that screen – the lack of a touchpad. The button initially used to replace it is very small and not as easy to touch as I’d like when opening up maps or menus in-game. Of course, you can just use one of the other shortcuts for this if you’re so inclined.

Recent findings suggest that however, it does mean if there ever is a game that utilises the touchpad, like Ghost of Yotei, for example, you’re kind of out of luck. Admittedly, there isn’t a huge number of games that utilise this feature, or have anything beyond a single-use touch, so most of the time, it’s a bit of a non-issue. However, it is something to consider if this is to be your main controller.

As is the case with these controllers – and the same with the last Nacon controller I reviewed – this thing doesn’t feature rumble on the PS5, meaning it’s severely lacking in the immersive department.

For a lot of people, that’s just not going to matter, but for me it’s an additional feature that always brings me back to the DualSense Edge – a pro controller with full haptics and adaptive triggers. What’s even worse is that there is actually a rumble motor in this controller, but it’s limited to use on PC.

I can’t knock the controller too much for that because outside of the DualSense Edge, most pro controllers won't feature any form of rumble. It’s just a shame because, for me, if it had rumble on PS5, it would be among my favourite controllers.

Despite my musing over a lack of rumble support on PS5, I do think the Rev5 is worth considering if you’re in the market for a pro controller.

It feels fantastic in the hand, with a satisfying click and travel to each of its buttons; the customisation is easy to change from a software perspective, but also incredibly accessible from a hardware perspective.

It features great build quality, the charger/dongle system is handy, and it comes with a pretty cool carry case. And you get all of this for about £20 to £30 less than most other pro controllers.

Is it perfect? No way. But it’s a pretty damn nice controller.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, bari Weiss’ tenure as the editor-in-chief of CBS News has sparked a myriad of responses from media pundits and the general public, who’ve taken problem with the organization’s content. While Weiss has received praise in some circles, she’s also been critiqued for some of her decisions, including those made in regard to 60 Minutes. Even now, some continue to chastise her editorial and staffing choices for the news magazine show. All the while, it seems Weiss is embroiled in some reported drama involving another news program.

In a recent development, just recently, Weiss was at the center of a report involving Face the Nation, one of CBS News’ key political programs. According to this update, Weiss apparently planned to part ways with the aforementioned show’s moderator, Margaret Brennan. The media newsletter Status (via The New York Post) didn’t specify why Weiss opted to retain Brennan. At this point, Brennan has headlined FTN since 2018 and, in addition to that she serves as the network’s chief of foreign affairs and fills in as an anchor on CBS Evening News.

Recent findings suggest that although Brennan is still with the show, it just lost two key members of its team. Senior executive producer Mary Hager recently announced that she would depart CBS News after 25 years with the network. Another key detail about this move is that since 2022, Hager has served as the executive director of politics for the Eye Network and has overseen its Washington Bureau. FTN executive producer Anne Hsu is leaving the show but, unlike Hager, she’ll remain with CBS and will head up its Hong Kong bureau.

These major exits mark the end of another era for Face the Nation, which debuted back in 1954 and, as of right now, it’s unclear just how Weiss will proceed in regard to filling those posts. With this, the Free Press founder finds herself in another staffing situation just months after her overhaul of 60 Minutes. And that series of personnel changes is still being discussed as part of the backlash that 60 has received as of late.

Ex-60 Minutes EP On His Biggest Concerns Amid Bari Weiss’ Leadership: ‘That Would Have Freaked Me Out’.

Earlier this year, Anderson Cooper exited his correspondent post at 60 Minutes after nearly two decades, citing a desire to have more time to spend with his loved ones. It was subsequently reported, however, that Cooper’s departure was partially due to disagreements with Weiss. Shortly after Cooper’s move, Weiss and series EP Nick Bilton fired correspondents Cecilia Vega and Sharyn Alfonsi along with former EP Tanya Simon and several others. Correspondent Scott Pelley was also fired days later after reportedly accusing Weiss of “murdering” the show.

Recent findings suggest that in the aftermath, Weiss brought in a roster of new talent to join series veterans Lesley Stahl, Bill Whitaker and Jon Wertheim. Pundits like Ross Douthat, Ariel Levy and Sir Trevor Phillips were brought in to fill out the staff. All the while, Weiss continues to receive backlash for those staffing changes, and she’s also been on the receiving end of news bias allegations (which she’s denied). Additionally, 60’s low ratings amid Season 59 have also been a point of contention among critics.

Bari Weiss addressed the 60 Minutes concerns just weeks ago and claimed the show had been doing “tremendously well.” Several staffers including Tony Dokoupil and Norah O’Donnell have also defended Weiss against backlash. In terms of Face the Nation, it’ll be interesting to see how Weiss plans to tap for those big producer jobs. Time will also tell whether Weiss chooses to revisit her reported strategy to cut ties with Margaret Brennan.

  • First up, a new character: The Fool!
  • Recent findings suggest that there are also two fresh game modes to try out with this beta upgrade.

In a recent development, hark! A new Slay the Spire 2 patch is here! Or, well, it is if you're someone who's trying out the beta branches of the game. If you're not, it might be worth trying out, as Mega Crit say this is their biggest patch for the game so far, with "some really impactful bits of content that will require lots of testing before they reach the main branch.".

First up, a new character: The Fool! "Wah!! The first new character for Early Access arrives!" a Steam blog post explains. "A silly musician who wields a bow! How can such a whimsical creature survive within the Spire? Why, that's up to you! We expect to make a great number of content and balance changes before the Fool is ready for the main branch. Even more importantly, be sure to have fun figuring out all the strategies and story of this gently bard. It would be foolish not to!" The post doesn't go into much detail as to what the new character can actually do, so, you'll have to discover that one for yourself!

Recent findings suggest that there are also two fresh game modes to try out with this beta upgrade. The first is Blitz, a "condensed and chaotic deckbuilding-focused mode." Here, the "Merchant's wares feel a bit off, the map is gone, and Gold no longer matters." You'll also find it comes with five levels of Ascension shared across every character, and you can unlock it by completing an Ascension run on any difficulty. The second mode is Dread, which as the name implies, is a "brutal" difficulty mode that you can only play if you've reached Ascension 10 on every character, including The Fool. "All ascension modifiers are enabled. Bosses are stronger and buff all enemies in their Act. Curses will also pile up as you climb the Spire. Death is expected.".

In a recent development, you can expect a bunch of upcoming balance tweaks and changes too. For starters, you'll find that rest sites can now appear a floor earlier every act. New events have been added to Underdocks and Act 2 and 3 too. Some nice quality of life alterations have been made, like how the character select screen for standard runs will start on whatever character you played as last, and controller navigation at the Merchant has been improved too. You can read all about the rest of the many changes right here.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xbox leader Asha Sharma has alluded to harnessing the power of generative AI when making games, in a memo published this afternoon.

Sources indicate that the memo, titled 25 years of Xbox, charts the growth of Microsoft from small beginnings through to the thousands-strong firm it is today. But it's Sharma's comments at the end of the memo that are of particular interest.

According to recent reports, while talking about what the next 25 years could bring, Sharma lamented that "too many ideas never become games" and that "too many games fall short of what their creators imagined". "For decades, this has been the unavoidable tradeoff of ambition," she wrote. "We must change this.".

Sharma continued: "Throughout human history, the scale of what we could create was determined by the people, capital, and resources we could command. That relationship is beginning to break. A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations. A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers and hundreds of millions of dollars. And our largest studios will be able to pursue ambitions as far beyond today's games as Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is from its first entry in 1982.".

It has been revealed that there is no explicit mention of generative AI here, but the language is suggestive - "a single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations". Furthermore, Asha's memo follows last month's announcement of an Xbox Labs initiative that also sounded like it was based around generative AI, despite avoiding the phrase specifically.

Industry observers note that this isn't a surprise, of course. Microsoft as a wider organization is all-in on generative AI, with Copilot, and Sharma's background at Microsoft is in AI. But it's an area she's avoided speaking too enthusiastically about since her hiring as Xbox boss earlier this year. At the time, Sharma said she has "no tolerance for bad AI", and there's been such a lot else going on in the months since - including wide-ranging restructuring resulting in the loss of thousands of Xbox jobs - that the topic of generative AI has fallen into the background. Perhaps now we're seeing the sprouting seeds of it.

We've asked Microsoft for clarification.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A Bloomberg report says Civilization studio Firaxis has laid off roughly 60 people, representing about one-third of its total headcount. Heather Hazen, who took over as studio head in 2023 after more than 25 years with Firaxis, is also leaving.

It has been revealed that A 2K Games spokesperson didn't comment on the reported number of employees let go, but confirmed that layoffs had occurred in a statement provided to PC Gamer. "Firaxis is restructuring and recentering around the studio’s core strength — designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years," the rep said.

Recent findings suggest that "As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis. These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis.".

The rep also confirmed that Hazen has stepped down as Firaxis studio head: "With the studio entering this reset, she feels this is the right, deliberate moment to hand over the reins to ensure the next studio leader has full ownership of this newly introduced era from the start.".

According to recent reports, firaxis has enjoyed great success as the developer of the Civilization and XCOM games, but it's struggled in recent years. Marvel's Midnight Suns was critically acclaimed but sales were middling, while Civilization 7 was just middling overall: Despite a raft of updates and changes since its 2025 release, its user rating on Steam remains stubbornly "mixed" while player numbers are still well behind that of Civilization 6.

That's resulted in previous rounds of layoffs: Roughly 30 people were let go in 2023, while an unknown number were cut in 2025. The Bloomberg report indicates a latest XCOM game in development at Firaxis has also struggled and missed a major milestone earlier this year; work on the game will reportedly continue but may face changes as a result of the layoffs.

Last night, Xbox Game Studios and Halo Studios have revealed a free enhancement for the recently-released Halo: Campaign Evolved, which promises to add the four-player co-operative PvE mode, Firefight, to the game.

In a recent development, "For nearly two decades, Firefight has been a Halo favorite, challenging Spartans to team up, hold the line, and survive wave after wave of enemies," claims Halo Studios director of competitive engagement Tahir Hasangjekaj stated in a dedicated post on the Xbox website. "The tradition continues this winter as we add the four-player cooperative PvE mode to Halo: Campaign Evolved in a free update.".

Though we don't have a release date for the update yet, Hasangjekaj does explicitly state "this Winter" as a window, and promises that we'll hear more information about the update at Halo Fest - due to run from 12th to 13hth December in Seattle, Washington. My money would be on a release around then, therefore.

"We're kicking things off tonight at Xbox FanFest, where attendees will be the first to jump in and experience Firefight across latest maps and armed with plenty of weapons to help even the odds." It seems there's already a playable build of the mode, then.

It's worth noting that this is quite an odd news blast from Xbox, since the last official information we heard about the Halo brand was that the next major Halo game being developed by Activision, as Halo Studios all but closes as part of Microsoft's Xbox 'restructuring' that saw one key member behind Halo: Campaign Evolved promoted and laid off within the same week. As things stand, we don't know anything specific about the future of the series, but there are plenty of rumours that the next title will be a reboot developed by Call of Duty's Sledgehammer Games.

It's been fairly busy 24 hours for Xbox: as well as this Halo update, we've heard from Asha Sharma as she celebrated the 25th anniversary of Xbox by seemingly going all-in on Gen AI. Elsewhere, we got the announcement that Wolfenstein 3 is in development over at MachineGames, headed up by Hugo Martin.
