It was around the 80-hour mark that the panic started to set in. I thought I had done and seen it all. Ran narcotics across the Leonida Keys. Exiled myself from Port Gellhorn. Fought bikers in Ambrosia. Joined a cult. Robbed banks. Partied. I created a life worth living in the heart of Vice City.

Jason and Lucia's story may have been over, but an adventure of my own was just beginning. While I had accomplished a lot in GTA 6, I never did find the time to refuel my beloved '65 Vapid Dominator and drive the long, winding roads up to Lummox County. It's astonishing to think so much time could be spent exploring Leonida, only for its northern border to remain something of a mystery.

Then again, there are still so many mysteries left for me to solve.

It has been revealed that so many incidental interactions that have the capacity to spiral into pure carnage. Diversions to discover that may lead to utter disarray. There are streets I've yet to set foot on, and shops I still haven't visited in my hours-long search for a quality leather jacket. There's at least one financial institution that I haven't yet figured out how to escape from without five-stars' worth of VCPD officers shooting me to smithereens.

Industry observers note that I fear I may never see or experience all that this world has to offer. And yet, after 13 years of waiting for a newly introduced Grand Theft Auto game, perhaps that's the way it should be.

Recent findings suggest that going from a fan at GTA 4's midnight launch to professionally covering the series has been a career highlight, including reviewing GTA 5 in X360 magazine. I'm never more than a few moments from diving back into Rockstar's worlds. After finishing GTA 6's story, I'm now well past 100 hours still exploring Leonida, using a PS5 Pro code provided by the publisher. – Reviewer Josh West.

It has been revealed that there are precious few development studios who are willing to play in these sorts of contemporary urban environments. Such is the inherent complexity of regulating an underlying simulation where even the simplest act creates such a wide array of possible consequences. Rockstar Games hasn't just set a upcoming benchmark; it has delivered what is undoubtedly the highest-fidelity sandbox in existence.

In a recent development, how Rockstar has been able to build something of this scale, scope, and quality will be dissected for years to come. It's easy to marvel at the near total lack of loading screens, the speed of character switching, and an exceedingly stable performance with minimal pop-in – despite absurd population density and the speeds at which you may traverse such a topographically diverse playspace.

These aspects are certainly impressive, but they aren't what ultimately elevates GTA 6 into being such a singular experience. Rather, there's a maturity behind the ethos of its core mechanical design, a cohesion in the way that its systems combine, which helps separate it from what the studio has accomplished in the past. In GTA 6, you can feel Rockstar's relentless pursuit of iteration, and the studio's ambition to create the most grounded instalment of the Grand Theft Auto franchise to date.

In a recent development, GTA 6 has the potential to be exceedingly divisive, particularly for those whose only point of interaction with the series thus far has been GTA 5. The life of crime you build for yourself in Leonida is far less chaotic and caustic than the adventures splattered throughout the streets of San Andreas. If the 2013 instalment was a faint echo of a Michael Bay blockbuster, then its successor is more Michael Mann – no less entertaining, but more considerate in how action feeds carnage and frames characters.

Recent findings suggest that jason Duval and Lucia Caminos – partners in crime, ensnared in a criminal conspiracy that quickly outstrips their understanding of an underworld that they once played in for idle thrills. The dual-protagonist foundation works exceedingly well for GTA 6, allowing you the space to grapple with two distinct personalities who are, in a sense, eternally bound to one another. You get to decide why that may be on a daily basis – for family, for honor, or for the simple promise of a bigger payday.

Industry observers note that the interplay between the two characters – born through a combination of nuanced writing, strong performances, and intricate character animations – feeds what is perhaps the most realistic and adult portrayal of a romantic relationship in video game history. Everyday acts of kindness bring Jason and Lucia together, indifference drives them apart. This isn't captured as part of some tawdry in-game checklist, but through deliberate, empathetic actions.

Everyday acts of kindness bring Jason and Lucia together, and indifference drives them apart.

In a recent development, in GTA 5, all that L2 was ever good for was aiming a weapon – in GTA 6, it also lets you hold hands with your partner. Interactions only get more detailed from there. Check in with each other over the phone, hit the gym together, hustle drunks at bars, or raid banks with his-and-hers matching tactical rifles. The connection you organically foster between the two characters (or allow to decay) only fuels a more considerate narrative that acts as a catalyst for endless free-flowing excursions across Leonida.

It has been revealed that the thematic coherence necessitated by the narrative arc acts as a foundation, feeding other critical changes to the way Grand Theft Auto has traditionally played. If Jason and Lucia's relationship feels real, then so too should the world they express themselves within.

You can only carry two handguns and two longarms at a time, for example, and brandishing a weapon will cause the public to react in different, volatile ways. Police presence isn't some glorified cone of vision, but rather it works as a communicative force to be feared – able to track your appearance, vehicles, and criminal activities between city limits. All of this (and more) contributes to a feeling of true, immersive role-play within Leonida.

Recent findings suggest that with Red Dead Redemption 2, Rockstar Games sought to create a reactive virtual world. The studio aspired to near-total immersion – action, interactions, and character development feeding off the sandbox's simulation of an everyday reality. In that sense, GTA 6 is a true sequel to RDR2. Rockstar has pursued relentless iteration of those Old West foundations here, leaning into those immersive qualities where it makes sense for the criminal-fantasy GTA fosters, and pulling back when they don't.

Industry observers note that unlike RDR2's Arthur Morgan, your hair and beard won't naturally grow over time. Weight and health fluctuations are less severe. Eating and exercising will impact the definition of Jason and Lucia's bodies, and resting helps to ease the exhaustive toll of constant criminality, but you'll never find yourself entirely at the mercy of these systems. Engagement with the Vice City lifestyle simply helps further the feeling that you are living life on your own terms.

Rockstar has gone to great lengths to inject more "freedom and flexibility" into its main mission design, all in an effort to reduce the number of fail states you encounter for daring to be experimental.

GTA 6 also features a more nuanced version of the Red Dead Redemption 2 honor system, with your reputation fed throughout the world more organically. It's one of the more fascinating upcoming systems, and a sharp diversion from prior games in the series that have never really commented on your criminality. Criminal Profiles are built gradually over time, ranging from Professional to Irredeemable, based on the way you commit crimes and handle pressure.

Sources indicate that the improvements to graphical fidelity and animation quality, and the lengths Rockstar has gone to create a virtual world with a functioning ecology, have meant that there are more human reactions from the populace to your presence than ever before. This intersects well with the Criminal Profile system, which (while never overly judgemental) does gradually convince you to define a moral compass and follow your own value system.

Industry observers note that there was a point where I realized that I had inadvertently sunk the entirety of my BuckMe bank account into an arsenal dedicated entirely to stealth action. I was raiding banks, drug labs, and gang compounds like GTA 6 was some sort of perverse Florida-set Metal Gear Solid. Sneaking my way into cover and onto rooftops, tracing enemy patrol patterns with a cigarette in one hand and silenced pistol in the other. I'd like to tell you that smoking before every firefight was because it temporarily boosts the Focus bar, but at some point I had become addicted to the aesthetic of it all.

Industry observers note that A stealth-action approach to encounters in GTA 6 worked in my favor because I was pursuing a Professional criminal profile – assigned by the worldwide reputation system for those who lean towards non-lethal incapacitations and clean getaways. I gravitated towards this style of play because of the Focus system, which iterates smartly on aspects of RDR's Eagle Eye and Max Payne's Bullet Time. Skillfully shooting weapons out of hands, or capping enemies in the knee before watching them tumble down staircases in slow motion, is just as satisfying as striding out of cover with a shotgun.

In a recent development, combat is one of many aspects where Rockstar has built precipitously beyond GTA 5. Placing bullets requires real aiming and precision. Weapon feedback is weighty, with each weapon type and manufacturer variant carrying its own unique handling profile. Survival requires movement and cover. Improvements have been made to the driving models too, with narrower streets necessitating more dexterity behind the wheel – not to mention countless more variables at play, from the threat of running out of fuel to the scores of modifications that can be applied to your favorite cars.

Sources indicate that there are degrees of sophistication to everything that GTA 6 does. There isn't an aspect of the series' gameplay that hasn't been improved over past instalments. It's a little slower and certainly more balanced, but no less entertaining. It's immediately noticeable that the artificial intelligence guiding the actions of both your partner and the NPCs who inhabit Vice City is greatly improved too, with some of GTA 6's best moments coming as you ask Jason to take the wheel while you lean out of a window as Lucia, a chattering assault rifle chewing through the tyres and rotary blades of a pursuing police force.

According to recent reports, if more nuanced storytelling has the potential to be divisive, then the revisions to the Wanted and Heat systems could be downright controversial. The police are more attuned to your actions than ever, actively tracking a number of variables at any one time in an effort to curtail crimes both substantial and small.

The return of a six-star wanted level is great for those looking for more of a challenge, although the Heat system – which can identify you after a crime based on factors such as your appearance, vehicle, outfit, visible weapon, partner's appearance, and whether you were recorded by CCTV – introduces a whole new dynamic to Grand Theft Auto. Some will love it, others will hate it.

This system can fluctuate between being a little frustrating (particularly at lower Wanted levels, for more incidental infractions) and utterly thrilling once the pressure is on, particularly if you're holding hundreds of thousands of dollars in stolen jewellery, marked bills, and narcotics between Jason, Lucia, and the storage of their personal vehicle – loot is lost if not properly funnelled through fences. And when the Heat and Wanted system are on your back, it evokes this almost desperate pressure to survive a city that is collapsing in on you.

Recent findings suggest that there's a sort of useful friction introduced through the revised Wanted and Heat system, overlapping with more freeform opportunities presented throughout the world itself. While GTA 5 is best remembered for its cinematic, structured heists, its successor finds its best moments as you decide on a whim to stick up a gas station or start smashing up the display cabinets in a jewelry store whilst you're between objectives. Bank robberies present massive opportunity and carry enormous risk, necessitating careful, tactile preparation before you burst through doors with weapons raised.

Recent findings suggest that the high-speed pursuits which can unfurl out of these encounters get gradually more out of control until they don't – Busted, Wanted, or free to fight and love for another day. Your Heat level and the world's awareness of your crimes is tracked intuitively on a more dynamic HUD, and I appreciate just how many opportunities there are to escape the police depending on any number of external factors.

Recent findings suggest that one of my favorite escapes saw me fleeing a large bank in Downtown Vice City – a densely populated area with streets packed full of police, pedestrians, and other vehicles. Throwing stash bags to my partner, spilling out of the vault and onto the streets, I was able to gain just a little distance from the cops and pull into a multistory carpark. Precious seconds to hide Jason's weapons in the trunk of his car, swap out Lucia's outfit, and hotwire a newly introduced vehicle. Clambering into the car, I manually shut off the headlights and engine, and ducked beneath the steering wheel – the patrolling police passed none the wiser, affording me the space to slip out of the garage slowly.

According to recent reports, the sheer scale of Leonida is something to behold. It's a playspace which rewards curiosity and creativity. It's impressive, especially when you remember it has all been "curated, considered, and created by a human hand.".

It's these sorts of unscripted sequences where GTA 6 shines brightest, although that isn't to say that the main story isn't packed with its fair share of memorable moments. There will be some debate as to whether the standout GTA 6 heists rise to the levels of GTA 5's 'The Paleto Score' and GTA 4's 'Three Leaf Clover', but they certainly come close.

Industry observers note that core mission design is still cinematic and largely linear by design, although you do have wider space to experiment in approach and escape than in previous Grand Theft Auto games – mission parameters can be broad, and it's up to you to decide how to achieve them. Rockstar has introduced the ability to manually retry a mission from its last checkpoint, further exorcising some of the series' more frustrating demons.

According to recent reports, GTA 6 also happens to be exceedingly well-written. Missions may be grounded in the virtual reality of Leonida, but they still have scope to be ridiculous. Mysteries unfurl from QR codes embedded in the world. Snippets from a radio news broadcast can make you laugh in one moment and pay off as a chance encounter in the world some 40 hours later. Random citizens will make you laugh, moments between Jason and Lucia will make you cry. It's a true joy to spend time in this world.

It has been revealed that I have Jason and Lucia start their road trip up to Lummox County in Key Lento, just a short drive to the federal penitentiary where they had once served time. Now, it's just the open road. Their favorite outfits packed into the trunk of an over-torqued Vapid Dominator, along with a small arsenal of weapons, ammo crates, body armor, and parachutes.

According to recent reports, the sun shines brightly; the radio tuned to V-Rock as hits from the '80s soundtrack a transition from lush ocean views to the quiet character of Hamlet. A quick stop at Sara's Unisex Salon for a fresh cut for Jason, and makeover for Lucia. Later, an unintended diversion into Southside after a small collision on Interstate 97 led an aggravated driver to jackknife my whip and feed bullets into the windshield – a local Pay 'n' Spray draining what little Pocket Cash I had on me for repairs. The sun started to set.

I stop to refuel somewhere around Vice City's Little Cuba district. An eruption of rain washing Lucia's makeup down her face, her gaze fixed entirely on another bay at the garage – a drunk driver pours gasoline into the flatbed of his truck. On the road and out of the city, the subtle changes in landscape reveal a world of contrast and contradictions. The changing colors of police vehicles, the different accents and demeanours of everyday citizens at roadside restaurants, indicate a crossing of boundaries.

Day transitions to night, night back to day. The weather shifting constantly. The vehicle splutters as roads become more uneven the further we cruise away from the big city. I switch from driver to passenger, smoking cigarettes as Jason and Lucia chatter about their lives. Eventually, vast farmlands settle into dense forest canopies beneath the shadow of Mt. Kalaga National Park. It took me 80 hours to see the dense foliage and lush, leafy green hues of Lummox County. And there's no telling how many more hours await me there.

In a recent development, my GTA 6 review was written based on a PS5 Pro playthrough, with the game code provided to me by Rockstar Games. And it must be mentioned, the improved ray tracing to help bolster lighting and shadow on PS5 Pro is pretty damned delightful. Vice City looks gorgeous at night.

In a recent development, so long as we're clear that I reviewed GTA 6 on PS5 Pro. I was very impressed with the performance. Rockstar targeted 30fps on all platforms, but I didn't encounter any fluctuations. There was infrequent pop-in, but that was only during play sessions which stretched beyond eight hours.

I spent over 100 hours playing GTA 6 for review. The Jason and Lucia story is all wrapped up, all optional missions are done, and I've made some pretty good headway on getting through a lot of the activities. Time to hunt for some collectibles!

I have completed every Grand Theft Auto game. Yes, even the ones released for PS1. I have very fond memories of attending the midnight launch for GTA 4, and even fonder memories of reviewing GTA 5 way back in 2013 for X360 Magazine.

It has been revealed that this will be a contentious debate, but there's a very good argument to be made that Grand Theft Auto 6 is the best Rockstar game. It's certainly a better overall experience than GTA 5, and more entertaining than Red Dead Redemption 2.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Legend of Zelda was in "dire straits" before Breath of the Wild gave the beloved series a massive second wind, according to two former Nintendo marketing leads.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's most recent remake has been a mega success, becoming the fastest-selling Switch 2 game so far, but the shiny upcoming adventure has also prompted some online debate over where the series should go next. Should Zelda lean into its carefully directed history - like the one brilliantly remade in Ocarina of Time - or keep the ball rolling with Breath of the Wild's wide open, spontaneous sandbox?

Nintendo of America's ex-director of social media marketing Kit Ellis and former public relations manager Krysta Yang chimed in on the discourse in their latest podcast (below), and explained that Zelda wasn't doing too hot before the Switch era.

"There has been some revisionist history out there lately," Ellis said in response to fans who reckon "the Zelda team ripped away" series staples, like classic dungeons and linear worlds, at the height of their popularity.

"I remember, I was going to the focus groups where it was a really dark moment," Ellis continued. "The feedback was like, 'The fan base is dwindling. This is not bringing in latest players.'".

The Legend of Zelda was supposedly "shrinking," while "interest in the audience was getting smaller and smaller" with each fresh entry. "They had to do something dramatic," Ellis mentioned.

"This series was in dire straits. They were selling, like, nothing," Yang added.

The Zelda series was certainly never irrelevant, but there's a pretty big gap between the roughly 8m copies Twilight Princess sold at the beginning of the Wii generation, the roughly 3m copies Skyward Sword sold at the end of the console's life, and the 34m copies that Breath of the Wild sold just one console generation later.

It was a success so big it spawned a wildly ambitious sequel, Tears of the Kingdom, and even influenced the latest 2D Zelda, Echoes of Wisdom. Now that classic Zelda's back in the spotlight, though, I do hope Nintendo's able to slot the series' curated dungeons into whatever the next mainline game becomes.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that even in the latter stages, with a full kit of precisely four ranged spells, Death’s Door is a simple proposition.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Declaring a Best Way of Doing Things is a fool’s game, though in recent years my favourite entries in the Tricky Hitting genre – inclusive of soulslikes and their hybridised disciples – have been the major, bulging ones. Elden Rings and Silksongs, with vast kingdoms and deep, rattling toolkits for surviving them. The reason it’s a fool’s game is because you can also have something like Death’s Door, a taut, compact, lighthearted little actioner that fills eight hours instead of 80 and yet never feels underwhelming or compromised for it.

It has been revealed that even in the latter stages, with a full kit of precisely four ranged spells, Death’s Door is a simple proposition. You are a crow. You hit things. Occasionally you shoot things. You collect the souls of a frog, a yeti, and a grandmother. Everything in-between directly relates to finding the errant monster/pensioner, or at a stretch, upgrading one of those four abilities.

It has been revealed that still, it’s clever with its limitations. Environments are small in number but vary wildly in tone and texture, and they tightly weave their paths into criss-crossing bundles that maximise travel – evoking the sense of a great, ranging adventure within relatively tiny spaces. The lack of a wiki’s worth of combat options also never becomes a problem, partly because it spreads out its spell unlocks, and partly because the smooth, flowing back-and-forths of its central swordplay are pleasurable enough to carry it anyway. Good bosses, too! They’re all characterful, memorable weirdoes who fight unlike anyone in their minion armies, and usually come with a hidden weakness to deduce and exploit.

According to recent reports, which is welcome, as these major lads and lasses do tend to launch difficulty spikes right up your feathered backside, and do so in a game that isn’t otherwise as fussed about trial-and-error pain endurance as some of its inspirations. They don’t, however, bring the mood down. At times, this tale of a pitch-black soul reaper working as an agent of Death (complete with an office of Death and embittered co-workers of Death) can get downright cosy, leading through you through warmly-lit jungles and breezy waterside ruins.

Industry observers note that recently replaying, I’d also forgotten how witty it can be. Little gaglets are sprinkled throughout, both visual and verbal, but the best jokes are saved for – funnily enough – the bosses, who’ll raise your pre-fight spirit with some amusingly terrible trash talk before becoming the punchline themselves. I audibly wheezed the first time a death animation immediately cut to the foe’s impromptu funeral, their beaked killer among the precious few guests. And even when the joke is recycled later, I couldn’t help tittering at the sight of my enemy – who seconds earlier, had been attempting to fatally sit on me – lying nobly in state.

Recent findings suggest that I previously considered ending my Valor Mortis review by calling it a gateway into the more demanding side of action-RPGs; a shorter, simpler alternative to FromSoft’s overwhelming titans that might nonetheless serve to introduce curious newcomers to their shared quirks and qualities. The game equivalent of splashing your chest with water before jumping into a pool. In hindsight, Death’s Door was always a better fit for that description, though there’s enough else here you don’t need to be prepping for something tougher to appreciate its lean, keen adventuring.

Industry observers note that now you—and the countless other people preparing to argue about this online—may have noticed that GTA 6 has been nominated for a number of awards despite the fact that it hasn't been released yet. In a press release, The Game Awards notes that jurors were in some cases provided with early access to enable awards consideration.

In a recent development, "There was a thing a few weeks ago where everyone thought that we had changed our dates to accommodate GTA, and it's like, no, actually our dates have been very set every year. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that where do you even start with a game like GTA 6?
  • We've all spent the last 13 years trying to figure out what GTA 6 might look like by the time it arrives, and the answer is perhaps more simplistic than some had theorised - it's basically GTA 5 mixed with Red Dead Redemption 2, but with a ton of added detail and ambition on top.
  • It has been revealed that before we get to the open world, which is surely the most incredible aspect of the entire game, we should first touch on the story of Lucia and Jason.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that where do you even start with a game like GTA 6? Not only is it the most highly-anticipated video game we've ever seen, but it's also attempting to live up to ridiculous expectations set by its predecessors over the years. GTA 3 revolutionised how we thought about 3D open-world epics, Vice City and San Andreas pushed things to the next level, GTA 4 took yet another massive step into the HD era, and GTA 5 propelled the series into another stratosphere.

We've all spent the last 13 years trying to figure out what GTA 6 might look like by the time it arrives, and the answer is perhaps more simplistic than some had theorised - it's basically GTA 5 mixed with Red Dead Redemption 2, but with a ton of added detail and ambition on top. That's all it needed to be, and I reckon people are going to absolutely love it.

It has been revealed that before we get to the open world, which is surely the most incredible aspect of the entire game, we should first touch on the story of Lucia and Jason. These two amateur criminals accidentally run into each other and establish a relationship (which can alter between platonic and romantic depending on how you interact throughout the campaign), and after a simple score goes wrong, they find themselves being dragged into more and more dangerous scenarios. That's the basic premise, and the rest is up for you to discover yourself.

The GTA 6 Extended Preview from a few months ago left me very concerned about whether there was enough intrigue to the two main characters (along with the NPCs for that matter), but I needn't have worried. Lucia is a fiesty, hot-headed personality - the type of person who thinks less about the consequences and more about the high life she's determined to acquire - while Jason is extremely laid back to a hilarious extent at times, although also highly capable in pretty much any situation he finds himself in. The two bounce off each other really nicely, and their dynamic definitely remains engaging throughout the campaign's duration.

Industry observers note that while I really don't want to spoil anything story-related, the mission structure is very much what you'd expect from GTA 5 and RDR2. In other words, there's a well-balanced mix of laid-back and humorous missions along with more intense shootouts and getaways that significantly ramp up in intensity. They've managed to get really inventive and ambitious with some of the later missions in particular, and I think there's no doubt they're the best of any GTA game.

I also want to point out the use of music in GTA 6's missions, which caught me off-guard and became one of my low-key favourite features. In a nutshell, if you find yourself in the likes of a shootout or a getaway, you'll often notice that curated tunes play in the background to amplify the situation. The developers sometimes even go a step further by making the lighting around you pulsate to the beat, or by introducing lyricists to create a menacing vibe, and it can turn an otherwise generic mission into an amazing one. Seriously, I can't overstate how much I love this feature.

The story itself takes 40ish hours if you completely rush it (which admittedly I've been doing for the most part to hit this embargo), but if you take your time and do at least a decent amount of the optional stuff, it's likely more around 60-100+ hours. As I say, I've enjoyed all of those hours, and I think the campaign seriously hits its stride in the final third - the vast majority of memorable moments are saved for the latter stages.

I don't want you to fixate on the 40-100+ hour figure though, and that's because GTA 6's open world is so incredible and so vast that you could be playing it for months, and likely years, and not see everything it has to offer. We've never seen a GTA world like this - traffic levels are extremely high, the number of NPCs on the streets is ridiculous, it always feels like something's happening around every corner (there are so many random encounters!), you'll find loads of buildings you can go into, there's so much detail on everything... it's just an absolute dream for anyone who loves the idea of immersing themselves in this game.

GTA 5 had an amazing open world too, but after going back and playing it for the purpose of this review, there are two major differences that stand out - there's far less actually happening in the world at any one time (and therefore much less to interact with), and the map just feels tiny in comparison. GTA 6's state of Leonida incorporates so much more than just Vice City itself, including many other highly-populated areas such as Key Lento and Ambrosia. The first time you actually see Vice City in a mission (assuming you haven't gone and explored it previously) is a highlight of the entire game - it immediately appears so vast and so incredibly detailed that it feels like a next-gen experience.

The way in which you interact with that world as a player has evolved as well. Cops are smarter than ever, and not only prove a tough challenge when attempting a getaway at three stars or more, but they also remember what you look like - and therefore you sometimes have to disguise yourself by changing into different outfits. Stealing a car now requires you to think about what kind of lock system it has on it, and whether there's a tracker fitted that will alert the police to your location. Cars can even run out of fuel now! Every element feels more in-depth than we've seen in GTA in the past, but Rockstar has crucially balanced the impact just right, so it's never to the detriment of your ability to just have fun.

In a recent development, I do think you'll get the most out of the game if you pace yourself though. It feels intentionally designed to encourage a slow playstyle where you explore, hang out, browse the fully-featured social media and news feeds on your phone (complete with video clips and comment sections), take part in games like pool and minigolf, engage in countless side-missions and random encounters, watch and play a ridiculous amount of purpose-built content on your in-game TV, and ultimately just see what you can discover without rapidly jumping from mission-to-mission. The amount of content here is overwhelming, but in a really satisfying way.

Of course, it's almost a given at this point that GTA 6 looks visually incredible, and I can confirm that it's definitely a stunner on Xbox Series X. There's some occasional pop-in, but it's minimal, and I only ran into a few tiny bugs during the review period (which may have been ironed out for release anyway). The performance is mostly very smooth considering the circumstances as well - yes, it's a bit jarring at first to go back to 30FPS if you've been playing 60FPS games for the most part in recent years, but give it an hour-or-two, and you probably won't care anymore. Seriously, it's a total non-issue for me at this point, and I'm more than happy playing at 30FPS.

It should be noted that I played around 30 hours on a VRR-enabled display during the review period, and around 10 hours without one. I was perfectly happy with the performance in both cases, with the only noticeably substantial frame rate drops occurring during very rare and visually intensive gameplay sequences.

So, is there anything I don't like about GTA 6? The only thing I'd say is that it doesn't top my tier list in terms of greatest GTA stories ever, although it's probably still in the top three. It's a narrative that'll fully invest most players from start to finish, and there are shocking moments and twists that are bound to last long in the memory, but I also reckon it gets a bit too convoluted and farcical at times. That mentioned, the final third of the campaign is jam-packed with intense story elements and incredibly action-packed missions, guaranteeing some truly jaw-dropping moments.

Its tone can also feel overly harsh and uncomfortably serious in specific circumstances, but hey... this is Grand Theft Auto after all. Every GTA has its moments like that, but the impact feels more striking this time due to the enhanced sense of realism. Fortunately, there's plenty of lighthearted humour to be found along the way as well.

Somehow, GTA 6 lives up to the hype. Rockstar Games has crafted the most incredible open world I've ever experienced in a video game, packed with so much detail that I'll want to continue exploring it for months and likely years to come. It's coupled with a campaign that's full of extremely entertaining missions, led by two main characters who I've become much more invested in than I'd anticipated.

I'd have been fuming if you'd told me in 2013 that I'd have to wait 13 more years for the next GTA game, but now that it's finally here, I'm just relieved they've somehow managed to pull off another Game of the Decade contender once again.

Boston Blue Season 2 has been chugging right along amid the 2026 TV schedule, and viewers have been treated to some serious action and tense family drama. Mae Silver’s re-election (for Boston District Attorney) campaign, Sarah Silver’s impending marriage to Seth Yates and the reunion of Reagan brothers Danny and Jamie are among the highlights thus far. The season has also been eventful for Lena Silver and, based on the latest episode, I think she may end up in a messy storyline, which I’d prefer not to see.

Sources indicate that sonequa Martin-Green’s Lena Silver has a busy career, and she also has an eventful personal life, which has been tackled again this season. One of the biggest plot points revolves around her relationship with Detective Brian Rodgers (Ryan Broussard). At the tail end of Season 1’s finale, Rogers was in a car accident (which fans learned in Season 2 was part of an orchestrated hit). While Lena and Brian rehabbed together following the former’s own gun injury, Rogers became restless due to not being cleared to work again.

Sources indicate that at the end of the episode, it was revealed that the flowers came not from Rogers but from Lena’s other ex-boyfriend, Dr. Troy Underwood, who was introduced in Season 1. It was established that prior to the events of the show, Troy and Lena dated, with the latter putting her life on hold to support him during medical school. That made it quite painful for Lena when Troy cheated on her during his training. Lena seemed to be done with the doctor but, amid this newest episode, she accepted a dinner invitation from him in order to hear him out.

In a recent development, so, with all of these plot threads in mind, my theory is that Lena and Troy will get closer and that Rogers will return to Boston after being assigned to a local DEA office. With that, Ms. Silver will find herself in the middle of a tense love triangle (and have to choose who she’ll want to bring to those Shabbat dinners). That’s the sense I’m getting, at least, but I’m hoping that’s not the case.

What It’ll Actually Take For Tom Selleck To Appear On The Blue Bloods Spinoff (Per Donnie Wahlberg).

It has been revealed that first off, love triangles – whether they’re featured in procedurals or not – have become incredibly ubiquitous and feel somewhat clichéd at this point. Given that, I would hope that Boston Blue’s writers can think of something more interesting to do when it comes to handling Lena’s love life. There are also more specific reasons why this specific triangle would be relatively odd.

It would be weird for Lena to legitimately re-enter a relationship with Troy due to how he hurt her. Yes, Lena is a rational person who can extend grace but, given her characterization, it just feels weird for her to even think about getting back with someone who wronged her in such a deep way. Plus, if faced with a decision between Troy and Brian, I just can’t see her not choosing the latter, as her glitch with Rogers amounts to a lovers quarrel. So, if Rogers comes back and is ready to accept help, why choose Troy?

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Whatever the case, I’m getting the feeling that Lena’s romance journey will greatly differ from that of Danny and his partner, Maria Baez. Here’s hoping Silver gets a nuanced relationship story as Boston Blue’s second season continues. 💡 Key Takeaways

  • New Game Plus, as mentioned below, raises the level cap to 100, and scales enemies and regions in the game around you.
  • There'll be upcoming versions of equipment with new stats to find, and they'll be labelled with "NG+" so you know when you've picked one up.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

ENHANCEMENT 17TH NOVEMBER: The Blood of Dawnwalker update 1.2 - the update that brings a Upcoming Game Plus mode, predominantly - is now available on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series S/X.

New Game Plus, as mentioned below, raises the level cap to 100, and scales enemies and regions in the game around you. Previously, the game was zone-scaled, so some zones were tougher than others. In New Game Plus, this will no longer be the case, so you can go and explore Xanthe's region at the back of Vale Sangora straight away, if you want to.

There'll be upcoming versions of equipment with new stats to find, and they'll be labelled with "NG+" so you know when you've picked one up. You can unlock New Game Plus from the main menu after choosing your base save and difficulty option. All of your accrued skill perks and abilities will be available to you at the start of the Withering Away quest in the game's prologue.

The full patch notes for Dawnwalker update 1.2 are:.

ORIGINAL STORY 13TH NOVEMBER: A Fresh Game Plus mode is coming to vampiric RPG The Blood of Dawnwalker next week.

Developer Rebel Wolves has now detailed everything coming with The Blood of Dawnwalker's Update 1.2, right now planned to go live sometime next week, and top of the list of changes is a Latest Game Plus for players who have already rolled credits on the game.

In a recent development, "If you completed the Epilogue, you can dive right back into Vale Sangora with Upcoming Game+," the developer revealed earlier today. "Your level, skills, and inventory will carry over." Rebel Wolves is upping the level cap to 100 for New Game Plus, which will also have items with updated stats and enemies "balanced and scaled uniformly across all regions.".

Elsewhere in Enhancement 1.2, the studio is making tweaks to "enemy health pools and how often they use their abilities during combat," and improving terrain geometry to allow for "smoother movement during combat and exploration." We'll need to wait for more comprehensive patch notes before finding out which enemies are getting spongier or flimsier, however.

While the incoming patch doesn't seem to be as beefy as the last - the one that added animal petting and an easier Story mode - it'll be a good way to sink your teeth deeper into a game that's already begging to be replayed, thanks to a time management mechanic that can drastically change any given run.

Sources indicate that the new game from some former The Witcher 3 veterans came out in September and seems to have been a hit. Eurogamer's The Blood of Dawnwalker review called the game a "familiar dark fantasy adventure, but one with bold and provocative ideas of its own, that's mostly, enormously successful.".

According to recent reports, kurabayashi previously worked as a game programmer at TAITO, where he served as main programmer on titles such as Darius Gaiden, Fighters’ Impact, and Vertexer. A memorial service is being planned in accordance with his family’s wishes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that mucky and disreputable kiosk game Probably Stolen – Cyberpunk Shopkeeper Sim is getting three big updates over the next few months that add extra starting scenarios, building on the existing wealth of goods, materials, vocations and techs. Those starting scenarios range from peddling human meat to running the finest cyber-frappucino stall this side of Tannhäuser Gate. There are no hard release dates, and the contents of each revision may alter, but developers Questing Goose Studio have shared some rough timeframes.

Coming up in mid-December, there's the Junker starting scenario, which I assume is all about trading scrap, rather than being a Prussian nobleman. You'll get a bespoke perk, new items, and the ability to hire, equip and send scavs on expeditions. This patch will also include some minor expansions for the Fence and Gunsmith vocations – the latter will be able to flog or otherwise make use of shotgun shells, 25mm grenade rounds and a tier 3 handmade SMG, alongside new armour.

Late January is when you'll "very likely" get the chance to be an Organ Dealer, care of the second major enhancement. "Players will start by buying different organs and fulfilling specific requests, and will later be able to grow or print organs," a Steam blog explains. You'll also be able to filter blood and remove diseases, with different blood types having different value modifiers. How will you get your hands on organs? By sending horrible black market thugs on foraging "expeditions".

Last but not least, the planned April enhancement will add the Street Food Vendor starting scenario. This lets you weave a livelihood around choice beverages and edibles from a range of cultures, supported by updates to the game's Aquaculture and Hydroponics tech. Sounds a lot cheerier than the organ trading racket, but then again, Probably Stolen will doubtless find a way to make it utterly grim. Guests at Sweeney's Cantina know better than to ask what our frappucinos are made of.

Sources indicate that are you playing Probably Stolen? It's been doing better than expected. I was keen on the demo, but my attention was lured away by a truly upsetting game about dogpeople in caves.

The Game Awards 2026 has just announced the nominees across all its categories, and sticking out like a sore thumb is GTA 6.

It's the odd one out, because it's the only game shortlisted that has yet to release. Despite the fact it isn't out yet — and even that reviews have yet to land — Rockstar's hotly anticipated game is nominated across numerous categories.

It has been revealed that in fact, it's the most-nominated game at this year's awards, with a total of eight nods if you include Manni L. Perez's nomination for Best Performance. It's up for the following trophies:.

Yes, on top of all its other nominations, GTA 6 is in contention for Game of the Year.

There has been much debate online about whether the game would be considered for The Game Awards at all, given how close its launch is to the event itself.

Many believed it would not receive any nominations, because the nominee announcement was set to occur before GTA 6 launches.

However, the voting jury — which comprises hundreds of gaming media outlets from around the world — has deemed the game worthy of recognition in eight categories, more than any other 2026 title.

What's clear is that many jury members must have played the game, but more interesting is that they clearly hold it in high regard if it's been shortlisted for so many awards.

This has been quite revealing, then; it's a major hint at what critics think of the game, and we now also know (officially) who is playing the role of Lucia Caminos, one of the two lead characters.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 is finally here. The long-awaited sequel arrives 13 years after the release of GTA 5 for PS3 and Xbox 360. It's a moment worth celebrating. Clearly, Rockstar Games feels the same way, as the studio's elusive co-founder and president makes a rare statement to help welcome you to Leonida.

"Rockstar Games was founded on the belief that games could achieve the same distinction as all other forms of storytelling, become essential to modern culture, and to be thought of as stories and worlds that live on with us," states Houser, in a comment released to GamesRadar+.

According to recent reports, "This week, Grand Theft Auto returns to Leonida and modern-day Vice City. While things have changed and time has passed, one aspect holds true: We have tried to create an experience that will exceed your expectations while showing what this medium is capable of, and why we believe games are so special.".

Sources indicate that houser has an executive producer credit on every mainline installment of the Grand Theft Auto series, and has served as a central creative lead and source of truth within the studio. He knows better than most just how crucial Rockstar's sprawling virtual worlds are to players, and the breadth of interest this return to Vice City will attract around the world. It's a challenge he doesn't take lightly.

According to recent reports, "Whether you can trace your journey to this game through the entire series or are experiencing Grand Theft Auto for the first time, this is a narrative set in a world of possibilities – and it is up to you as the player to shape how it ultimately feels, and concludes. We hope it feels both familiar and entirely new, and above all, we hope you have fun." Houser's statement concludes: "We look forward to many more years of sharing these experiences with you.".

Many more years is right. While Grand Theft Auto 6 has debuted as a single-player-only experience (and the studio is yet to officially comment on whether a successor to GTA Online is in development), I can say from my own personal experience with the game that it presents the sort of reactive world which will have the capacity to surprise and delight for years to come.

Netflix's long-gestating Magic: The Gathering animated series is called Planeswalker, and it's coming in 2027.

Sources indicate that the title was revealed at MagicCon Atlanta, and Netflix shared a first look at the show on Twitter/X on 13th November. "Every great story begins with a spark. Here's your first look at Planeswalker, a newly introduced animated series based on Magic: The Gathering. Coming to Netflix in 2027", the manufacturer wrote, and shared a teaser, which you can see below:.

Recent findings suggest that according to a synopsis shared with IGN, the series follows Chandra Nalaar, "a volatile pyromancer hunted for her gifts, and haunted by her past". It continues: "Confronted by an insidious force, Chandra and some of the most legendary Planeswalkers must harness their extraordinary abilities, navigate treacherous alliances, and battle their own inner demons to prevent a cataclysmic war that threatens to consume their very existence".

Netflix first announced a Magic: The Gathering series in June 2019, with Avengers: Endgame directors Joe and Anthony Russo attached, and it was originally due in late 2022. Two years in, the original showrunners departed over creative differences, and in September 2024, Netflix confirmed it had started again from scratch with Star Trek: Picard and 12 Monkeys showrunner Terry Matalas in charge.

IGN reports that Matalas, who most recently ran Marvel's VisionQuest, is running the show alongside Cindy Appel. Budapest-based studio DIGIC Pictures is handling the animation.

At the end of last month, we learned PUBG is also being turned into a live-action series for Netflix, with Donald Glover set to direct, write, executive produce, and star.

In a recent development, glover is a two-time Emmy and Golden Globe winner, best known for Atlanta and Community. Krafton calls PUBG "one of the world’s most enduring gaming franchises", and says the game, which is credited with popularising the battle royale genre, holds seven Guinness World Records.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • We've said previously that, for better or worse, the third-person sci-fi RPG Exodus looks a lot like Mass Effect.
  • I kid you not, this is not a name I've cooked up or run across on social media.
  • Femjun is a very direct reference to Femshep, the female version of Commander Shepard in BioWare's Mass Effect trilogy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We've said previously that, for better or worse, the third-person sci-fi RPG Exodus looks a lot like Mass Effect. It's a characterization that developer Archetype Entertainment isn't shying away from—in fact, it seems to be actively embracing it with the reveal of the game's female protagonist, who they refer to as Femjun.

I kid you not, this is not a name I've cooked up or run across on social media. It's right there on the Exodus website: "Meet Femjun! You’ve been waiting to see FemJun, and today we’re happy to say she’s finally here.".

Femjun is a very direct reference to Femshep, the female version of Commander Shepard in BioWare's Mass Effect trilogy. While the male version was effectively the default playable character through the first two games, BioWare took steps to put them on equal footing for Mass Effect 3. That effort included a vote to let fans decide the character's official face, which was subsequently used on alternate or inside covers of Mass Effect 3 packaging.

Voiced by Jennifer Hale, Femshep became so popular that when BioWare dropped the Mass Effect Legendary Edition trailer, it was she who appeared most prominently.

So, back to Exodus: Fenjum will be portrayed by Carina Conti, who's appeared in television shows including Tracker, Good Trouble, All Rise, and Winning Time: The Rise of the Lakers Dynasty. Exodus will be only her second videogame credit, though, following Mafia: The Old Country, in which she portrayed Isabella Torrisi. The male version of Jun will be played by veteran voice actor Stephen Oyoung.

Narrative director Drew Karpyshyn also confirmed that romances in Exodus won't be locked out based on whether you play male or female Jun: "We want to make sure that players can engage in what romances they want if you pursue them.".

Exodus is set to launch on April 7, 2027, and will be available for PC on Steam and the Epic Games Store.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A massive part of the point of The Blood of Dawnwalker is that you're on a fixed time limit.
  • It has been revealed that "If you completed the Epilogue, you can dive right back into Vale Sangora with Upcoming Game+!" a post from the devs explains.
  • In any case, the upgrade goes a tad further than that.

A massive part of the point of The Blood of Dawnwalker is that you're on a fixed time limit. You've got 30 in-game days and nights to try and save your family, and if you don't manage to see everything the game has to offer, well, the game's director is fine with that. But that doesn't matter as much now, as The Blood of Dawnwalker is getting its 1.2 update next week that adds in a fresh game plus mode.

It has been revealed that "If you completed the Epilogue, you can dive right back into Vale Sangora with Upcoming Game+!" a post from the devs explains. "Your level, skills, and inventory will carry over; the level cap will be raised to 100; enemies will be balanced and scale uniformly across all regions; and items will have NG+ versions with updated stats." Sounds like your usual new game plus affair! I suppose it is a good opportunity to try out different things compared to your first playthrough, but I'm not exactly aligned with the idea that the timer restriction is too restricting (as some mods have made clear how others feel that way).

In any case, the upgrade goes a tad further than that. If you got the Eclipse Edition of the game, the in-game soundtrack that came with it "will be extended with additional songs from the game." You can expect the soundtrack on streaming services soon, too. While details are slimmer here, there are also some planned balance changes, like updated enemy health pools and how often they use their abilities during combat, and terrain geometry has seen some improvements to allow for "smoother movement during combat and exploration.".

Overall, a bit of a smaller update compared to the last one, but one I'm sure will be welcome to some all the same. If you've not had a chance to check the game out yet and still feel on the fence about it, here's some lovely words from Mark's review: "There’s always that sense that something key or unexpected could be lurking around the next corner, to pull you into a quest dripping with depth and intrigue. It works to ensure the more busywork-esque tasks attached to angering Brencis and his Boyars never make Vale Sangora feel home to a string of boring boxes to tick. It’s a vibrant, constantly changing place with a thousand different threads metaphorically criss-crossing just beneath its surface, just as ancient ruins literally criss-cross beneath its swamps, crags, and forests.".

The first reviews for GTA 6 are officially out now, and as you've probably already seen, we've got one here at Pure Xbox! We gave the game an "Outstanding" 10/10, which isn't entirely surprising considering the history of this series.

Sources indicate that but what about everyone else? GTA 6 is nominated for Game of the Year at The Game Awards, so does it live up to that recommendation? Are the critics overwhelmingly enamoured with it? That's what we've been intrigued to find out.

So, here's what the critics are saying about GTA 6 so far:.

Recent findings suggest that "Somehow, GTA 6 lives up to the hype. Rockstar Games has crafted the most incredible open world I've ever experienced in a video game, packed with so much detail that I'll want to continue exploring it for months and likely years to come.".

"GTA 6 is the deepest, densest, most accomplished open world since Red Dead Redemption 2. Rockstar has set a fresh sandbox standard here, with a world that feels alive and populated with real people; Leonida is a place where it appears almost anything can happen at any time.".

It has been revealed that "A game so good I asked our tech team if I could somehow give it 11/10. GTA 6 is an absolute masterclass in genre-mashing. With meticulous detailing and levels of immersion that almost feel dangerous, it's steeped in steamy satire — with story beats that often cut close to home as they relish in laugh-out-loud absurdity. Given the state of the industry, it's sobering that we might never see another game like this again. Grand Theft Auto 6 is a cover-to-cover masterpiece without equal.".

Sources indicate that "Grand Theft Auto VI is a generational game that stands toe-to-toe with many of the great crime stories and satires across other media. It showcases both the entertainment value of interactive play and the current high-water mark for technical and artistic detail in games. Hunt for and count up all the minor faults or foibles you like, but then note how you just spent another hour lost in this remarkable escape into criminality, wanton violence, egregious sex, and the elusive potential of true love.".

It has been revealed that "This game is the culmination of everything the developer has previously achieved in the open-world space that pushes the genre to heights that, in all likelihood, no other developer will be able to reach. GTA 6 is an astonishing open-world action game that I’d wager won’t be outdone until Grand Theft Auto 7.".

According to recent reports, "GTA 6 is the highest-fidelity sandbox of its generation. Rockstar has built an open world of truly astonishing scale, scope, and quality. There's a degree of sophistication to everything GTA 6 does, and there's no aspect of the series' gameplay that hasn't been improved over past instalments.".

"I regularly find myself in love with video games, but it’s extraordinarily rare that I find myself in complete awe of them. Put simply, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played.".

According to recent reports, "A game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale, Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that.".

"Grand Theft Auto VI delivers a remarkably immersive and ambitious open-world experience, blending thrilling gameplay, diverse activities, and a compelling relationship between Jason and Lucia. While uneven storytelling, pacing challenges, and occasional performance drops prevent it from reaching perfection, the richly realized world of Leonida and its extraordinary attention to detail make this an unforgettable crime adventure that largely lives up to its monumental expectations.".

It has been revealed that "Grand Theft Auto VI is a great game that lives up to so much of the hype and expectations. Lucia and Jason are a well-written and compelling pair of protagonists, and the side characters you meet on their journey are great, even if the need to constantly raise the stakes across such a long story lessens its impact. You do have so much more freedom with how to tackle missions, though, and Leonida is a world filled with things to do and discover that will keep you coming back for a long time.".

As you can see, GTA 6 is a darling of the critics right now, and its initial rating on Metacritic sits at a whopping 99, which makes it the highest-rated game of 2026 (and literally the joint best game of all time if it keeps up this pace).

It has been revealed that it should be noted that the vast majority of reviews are for the PS5 version, but both the PlayStation and Xbox versions are both sitting at 99 as things stand. That figure will probably change, but not to any significant degree.

History tells us that we should have always expected a mainline Grand Theft Auto game to get incredible review scores, but it was really hard to see how they'd live up to expectations with this one. Nevertheless, they've somehow done it!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Call of Duty Endowment is marking Remembrance Day and its 17th anniversary by encouraging Modern Warfare 4 and Warzone players to pick up its Valor Pack, with all of Activision's net proceeds going towards helping veterans find jobs.

The Call of Duty Endowment Valor Pack - which has been available since Modern Warfare 4 introduced on 23rd October - was designed by the Endowment and Infinity Ward with US Marine Corps veteran and Medal of Honor recipient Kyle Carpenter in mind.

The items include a melee weapon blueprint inscribed with "Worth Fighting For", plus items called Relentless and Still Standing.

According to the Call of Duty blog, 100 percent of Activision's net proceeds from the pack (after VAT and sales tax) go to the Endowment.

To mark Remembrance Day, players who owned it and released either game before 6pm GMT on 12th November also received double XP tokens and a DMZ survival kit.

"Veterans bring incredible skills into the workplace after military service," said Carpenter.

The Endowment, which supports veterans in the UK as well as the US, indicates it has now helped place more than 180,000 into "high-quality jobs", and wants to reach 200,000 by 2030.

Other partners are also raising money, with Pilot's round-up campaign raising more than £4.7 million ($6 million) for the Endowment since 2019. Polaris will also donate around £19,500 ($25,000) if players collectively complete 5 million rides in its DAGOR vehicle across Modern Warfare 4 and Warzone by 25th November.

Sources indicate that it comes two weeks after Activision apologised to bereaved families of the Itaewon crowd crush victims and confirmed it would remove real footage of the tragedy from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. Players discovered that the game's opening cinematic uses short news clips to depict fictional civilian casualties during a North Korean invasion of South Korea. Those clips have since been found to include archive footage from the 2022 Itaewon disaster, in which around 160 people died.

Call of Duty's anti-cheat team Ricochet recently revealed it's officially cracking down on Warzone Agent.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that I knew Spider-Man: Brand New Day would make a ridiculous amount of money when it landed on this summer's 2026 movie schedule. What I didn't expect was to hear Sony's top movie executive making a serious case for Tom Holland's latest superhero adventure to earn a Best Picture Oscar nomination. But here we are, and apparently, the studio is prepared to put some real effort into making it happen.

Sources indicate that sony Pictures Motion Picture Group chairman and CEO Tom Rothman recently spoke with Variety about the movie's extraordinary success and why he believes it deserves Academy voters' consideration. With Brand New Day earning roughly $2.5 billion worldwide and breaking the domestic box office record, Rothman thinks there's something special about how audiences connected with Peter Parker's story. He explained:.

The reason it did as much business as it did is not because it's a superhero movie, it's because it's a super person movie.

I actually get what he's saying. While I enjoyed the action in Brand New Day, what stuck with me was how much of the movie focused on Peter's loneliness after the events of No Way Home. Here's a guy who can swing between skyscrapers and take down some of Marvel's most dangerous villains, but he can't get the people he loves to remember who he is. That's a pretty miserable situation, even by Peter Parker standards.

According to recent reports, audiences clearly responded as well. The film received overwhelmingly positive reviews. It also became the highest-grossing movie in North American box office history, an accomplishment I imagine Sony will mention quite a bit over the next few months. But does all that mean it deserves an Oscar nomination?

It has been revealed that rothman certainly thinks so. When asked whether or not a strong box office means Brand New Day should be a Best Picture contender, he responded:.

Once upon a time there were five best picture nominations, and then it was expanded to ten, to try to make room, I think, for quality commercial filmmaking… we’re biased, but we think [it should be nominated] so. We hope people will think about it.

Sony is backing up those comments with an actual campaign. According to Deadline, the studio has hired awards consultants and is planning special screenings and filmmaker Q&As beginning ahead of Thanksgiving. There's also talk of a theatrical rerelease designed to put the movie back in front of audiences and Academy voters.

Of course, superhero movies have historically struggled to crack the Best Picture category. Black Panther earned a nomination in 2019, followed by Joker the next year, but neither won. Even Christopher Nolan's The Dark Knight missed a Best Picture nomination, despite earning eight Oscar nods and winning two.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

As for Spider-Man, the character, he hasn't exactly been an Academy favorite. Sam Raimi's Spider-Man 2 won Best Visual Effects in 2005, while Into the Spider-Verse took home Best Animated Feature in 2019. Although no movie starring the web-slinger has ever competed for Best Picture.

In a recent development, still, I can understand Rothman's reasoning. Director Destin Daniel Cretton made a movie that made room for surprisingly intimate character moments, even amid all the enormous superhero spectacle. CinemaBlend's Jerrica Tisdale previously explained why that balance made the movie work so well, and I think it's a fair argument. Whether Academy voters agree is another matter entirely.

The nominations for the 99th Academy Awards will be revealed Jan. 21, 2027, and Brand New Day will have some stiff competition. After watching what Sony and Marvel accomplished with Peter Parker this summer, I'm certainly not going to dismiss the idea outright. Besides, if anybody deserves a little recognition after everything he's been through, it's Peter Parker. The poor guy could use a win.

Most Spider-Man movies, past and present, are available to stream with your Disney+ subscription.

Industry observers note that there's a truly astonishing level of detail presented all throughout Leonida. For all the pre-release conversation about whether Rockstar Games should have considered lowering the visual fidelity of its largest, most reactive sandbox to date in favor of performance boosts, the immersive qualities of this space are one of the standout aspects of GTA 6.

Industry observers note that I can say this with some confidence, having spent well over one hundred hours exploring Vice City in support of my spoiler-free GTA 6 review. In a statement released to GamesRadar+, the vice president of art and environment at Rockstar asserts that "the life is in the detail" of this astonishing open-world.

Sources indicate that "The subtle sway of trees or bunting swaying in the wind. A puddle of bin juice around the bottom of a dumpster, or an overgrown garden in a property that is unoccupied. The personalization of each home and business so that it all feels unique and there's no repetition," claims Adam Cochrane.

He adds: "Then add into that the vignettes and storytelling the teams have added for the players to explore and discover. Some of these areas have in-game rewards, and some are just rewarding experiences themselves when you see the care and attention that has gone into the creation.".

A lot of this detail is almost imperceptible, but it does all ultimately contribute to this feeling that you aren't playing as Jason and Lucia in the world that's been purpose-built to become a home to their criminal activities, but rather that you are living a life of your own design within a world that has some semblance of inherent virtual reality. It's a pretty astonishing thing to spend time in Leonida, as you'll no doubt discover for yourselves on November 19, 2026.

What's especially impressive is that GTA 6 arrives at a time where the video game industry is grappling with the spiralling pressures of creating games in the modern era – where increases in fidelity are placing more demands and expectations onto the shoulders of creative teams than ever before – and with the ethics of utilizing Generative-AI systems to help alleviate these burdens.

Sources indicate that cochrane is quick to remind us that the power of GTA 6 lies in the people who have brought this world to life. "Then you zoom out, and look at the sheer scale of the world, and you realize that the detail you've been discovering on such a small scale is quite literally everywhere across the vast landscape of this world. Then you realize that it's all been curated, considered, and created by a human hand," he says, before adding, "and you can't quite believe it.".

According to recent reports, as the launch draws even closer, we're covering absolutely everything you need to know about its PS5 launch, including preload options and release times. In this GTA 6 guide, we cover the GTA 6 release times.

Rockstar has confirmed GTA 6 will officially be playable from midnight on 19th November in your local time zone. If you have preloaded the game, it'll unlock at midnight, and then you can begin playing immediately.

As such, the game will unlock and be available first in Newly introduced Zealand. Availability will then roll out worldwide as each time zone reaches midnight on 19th November.

When the game debuts in the UK, we'll have a hub live on the home page documenting our coverage and providing a place for you to share your first experiences with GTA 6.

In a recent development, GTA 6 preload is available now! If you've pre-ordered from the PS Store, your download of the game should have started and will then be ready for you to start playing at release.

Rockstar has now officially confirmed the GTA 6 file size on PS5, and what you'll need to download, is 212GB. This is one of the biggest downloads and installs on console in history, and will probably only get bigger through patches and the addition of GTA Online.

GTA 6 will unlock and be playable in Latest Zealand first, as it's located in one of the furthest along timezones. The chances are New Zealand is further along in the day compared to wherever you live in the world, so yes, New Zealand will be the first to gain access to GTA 6.

It has been revealed that because of this, there's been a rising trend in people creating Latest Zealand PSN account to play games as soon as possible. This can be done with GTA 6 too, but you'll need to set up a fresh New Zealand PSN account and buy the game through its PS Store.

When you have done, you'll be able to play GTA 6 a few hours ahead of other countries like the USA. Keep in mind, though, that you can't transfer your save data from the Newly introduced Zealand account you set up to your normal profile.

If you were to play GTA 6 early via the Upcoming Zealand method detailed above, you get access to the game at these times:North America: 3am PST / 4am MST / 5am CST / 6am ESTUK/Ire: 11am GMTEurope: 12pm CET / 1pm EETAsia/Oceania: 8pm JST / 7pm AWST / 10pm AEDT.

GTA 6 is available digitally on the PS Store, or in a basic physical version that ships without a disc. The latter provides a code in the box that you redeem on the PS Store to get the digital version.

The two PS5 digital versions on offer are: Standard Edition and Ultimate Edition.

Ultimate Edition / Ultimate Edition Upgrade Contents:.

Rockstar is only selling GTA 6 in a digital format; you can't buy the game on a physical disc in any way. Even the version you buy in retail shops or from online retailers won't contain a disc. Instead, the actual GTA 6 box will have a code inside you can use to download the game. There's no version with a physical disc of any kind.

According to recent reports, rockstar has now confirmed a GTA 6 map will be made available, but it won't be included in the physical versions like for previous games. Instead, a physical GTA 6 map will be put on the official Rockstar store for $0.99. Or, it'll be included for free in all other purchases from the storefront.

I've not played it but it seems like a good take on the format. Clearly, though, sometimes you just need to play the hits, as a new release of the original game is on the way in the form of Super Meat Boy Again+, a remaster with updated graphics, levels and plenty more.

It has been revealed that what is there is very clearly Super Meat Boy, uh, again, just with a massive newly introduced lick of paint. There is probably some kind of joke to be made about it being DLSS yassified, but I'm too tired to think of one, so, you get the point. But it does look pretty good! I do kind of miss the Flash game aesthetic, I think there's a real charm to the sort of visual design sensibilities you'd find from that era, but this remaster certainly ain't ugly at least. Apparently it's not just the art that's new, as there's also new music, cutscenes, secrets and "stuff.".

According to recent reports, if the animated sequences featured in the trailer, which you can have a gander at above, are included in the final game that'll be a treat to watch too, as I think they better capture the Newgrounds pseudo sub-genre of animation than the graphical overhaul. It sounds like they will be looking at the Steam page, so, a treat to look forward to while committing an act of masochism by playing it!

There's no release date attached to this remaster, so we'll all just have to sit tight for an update there. The original is still listed on Steam, but if you fancy as significant a dose of nostalgia as the trailer is trying to present to you, you could always go play the original, plain old regular Meat Boy. It's playable right on Newgrounds thanks to the Flash emulator Ruffle and works like a dream! Or if you're happy to wait, you could always wishlist the new one on Steam.

Rainbow Six now sits under Vantage Studios, the Ubisoft subsidiary set up last year that also oversees Assassin’s Creed and Far Cry, and in which Tencent holds a 26.32 percent stake.

Recent findings suggest that last week, we learned that Ubisoft is reportedly working on two new Assassin's Creed games: one set in ancient Rome, and a mobile spin-off set in Jerusalem. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Crystal Dynamics has confirmed that eight people have been let go in the latest round of layoffs at the beleaguered Tomb Raider studio.

"Crystal Dynamics made a difficult, but necessary business decision to reduce our current studio staff by eight people," the studio said of the layoffs, first reported by Vertical Slice, in a statement provided to PC Gamer.

"Whenever we phase roles off a project, we make every effort to find new spots for our great colleagues first. Everyone affected receives a full severance package as well as job placement assistance to aid them through this transition. We wish them the best and hope to work together in the future.".

The studio added that no ongoing projects are impacted by the cuts.

According to recent reports, in terms of raw numbers, eight people is not a huge cut, especially when compared to layoffs at other studios—Firaxis reportedly cut roughly 60 employees earlier today, for instance. But it's concerning in the case of Crystal Dynamics because the studio has been bleeding for so long: This is at least the fifth round of layoffs in less than two years, and comes just eight months after the last round of cuts. Roughly 70 employees in total have been let go over that span.

It has been revealed that the studio has also struggled to get things done with its flagship series, Tomb Raider. Crystal Dynamics regained control of the property in 2022, shortly after the studio was acquired by Embracer, but in June Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis, a remake of the original game, was delayed to February 2027; less than two months later, the all-new Tomb Raider: Catalyst was pushed into 2028. The studio also co-developed the Perfect Dark reboot alongside The Initiative for four years before Microsoft killed it in July 2025.
